section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: North Dakota has one of the lowest minimum permit ages in the country. At what age can a teen apply for a learner's permit?
options: a:13,b:14,c:14 and a half,d:15
note: North Dakota allows teens to apply for a learner's permit at age 14 — one of the youngest permit ages in the country. This reflects North Dakota's rural character where driving skills are needed at a younger age for farm and ranch work.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What is the legal BAC limit for a driver age 21 or older in North Dakota?
note: North Dakota sets the per se DUI limit at 0.08% BAC for drivers 21 and older. Commercial vehicle drivers face a stricter 0.04% limit. Reaching 0.08% BAC is sufficient for a DUI charge regardless of whether the driver appears impaired.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: You are driving on a North Dakota rural highway and encounter a large grain truck moving slowly during harvest season. What should you do?
options: a:Pass immediately — farm vehicles must pull over for regular traffic,b:Follow at a safe distance and pass only when there is a broken yellow line and clear sight distance,c:Honk repeatedly to signal the truck to pull over,d:Pass on the right shoulder — farm vehicles always yield to cars
note: North Dakota's rural highways see significant grain truck traffic during harvest season. Follow at a safe distance and pass on the left only when: the centerline has a broken yellow on your side, you have clear sight distance of at least 1,000 feet, and no oncoming traffic is approaching.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: North Dakota's zero tolerance law for drivers under 21 sets the illegal BAC at:
options: a:0.00% — any detectable amount,b:0.02%,c:0.04%,d:0.08%
note: North Dakota's zero tolerance law sets an illegal BAC of 0.02% for drivers under 21. Any BAC at or above 0.02% results in automatic license suspension. Essentially, no alcohol is permitted for North Dakota drivers under 21.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What is the default speed limit on most North Dakota rural highways when no speed limit sign is posted?
options: a:55 mph,b:60 mph,c:65 mph,d:70 mph
note: North Dakota sets the default speed limit at 55 mph on unposted paved two-lane county and township highways (as well as gravel and dirt roads). Divided multi-lane highways are set at 70 mph, and rural interstates are set at 80 mph. Always watch for posted limits.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: You are driving on a North Dakota highway in winter and the road surface looks shiny and wet despite dry weather. This is likely:
options: a:A mirage caused by cold air,b:Black ice — a nearly invisible layer of ice that forms on road surfaces,c:Fresh road sealant that is still wet,d:Morning frost that will evaporate quickly
note: Black ice is a serious hazard on North Dakota's long, flat roads. It forms when moisture freezes on the road surface, creating a thin transparent layer that looks wet. Black ice is extremely slippery — if you suspect black ice, ease off the accelerator, avoid sudden steering, and brake very gently.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What must you do when a school bus stops on a North Dakota road with flashing red lights and an extended stop arm?
options: a:Stop only if you are directly behind the bus,b:All traffic in both directions must stop at least 20 feet from the bus on undivided roads,c:Slow to 10 mph and pass the bus if no children are visible,d:Stop only on divided highways
note: North Dakota requires all traffic on undivided roads in both directions to stop at least 20 feet from a school bus with flashing red lights. Wait until the lights stop and the arm retracts before proceeding. On divided highways with a physical barrier, only traffic behind the bus must stop.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What does North Dakota's Move Over law require when passing a stopped law enforcement or emergency vehicle?
options: a:Slow to 25 mph and stay in your lane,b:Move one lane away from the stopped vehicle if safely possible — or reduce speed if a lane change is not possible,c:Stop completely behind the vehicle until it moves,d:Move over only for law enforcement, not for tow trucks
note: North Dakota's Move Over law requires drivers to move one lane away from stopped emergency, law enforcement, roadside assistance, or highway maintenance vehicles with flashing lights. If moving is not safely possible, slow to at least 20 mph below the posted speed limit.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: On a North Dakota two-lane highway, which of these situations would make passing another vehicle ILLEGAL?
options: a:The road ahead is straight with a broken yellow center line on your side,b:There is a solid yellow line on your side of the center,c:The vehicle ahead is driving 10 mph below the speed limit,d:You have plenty of room to pass quickly
note: A solid yellow line on your side of the center line means passing is prohibited. You must not cross a solid yellow line to pass another vehicle regardless of its speed. Only pass when there is a broken yellow line on your side AND you have adequate sight distance.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: You are driving in a North Dakota blizzard with near-zero visibility. What should you do?
options: a:Turn on high beams to see further and maintain your speed,b:Pull off the road completely and wait for the storm to pass,c:Drive on the shoulder to avoid other vehicles,d:Follow the vehicle ahead very closely so you can see their tail lights
note: In a North Dakota blizzard with near-zero visibility, pull off the road completely — ideally at a rest stop or parking lot. Turn on hazard lights, stay in your vehicle, and wait for conditions to improve. Following other vehicles in whiteout conditions can lead to pile-ups when the lead vehicle stops.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What is the speed limit in a North Dakota school zone when warning lights are flashing?
options: a:10 mph,b:15 mph,c:20 mph,d:25 mph
note: North Dakota school zones have a speed limit of 20 mph when the warning lights are flashing or when children are present. Always reduce your speed well in advance of school zones and watch for children near the road during school hours.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Under North Dakota's implied consent law, refusing a chemical test after a DUI arrest results in:
options: a:No penalty — refusal is a protected right,b:A 180-day license suspension for a first offense,c:Only a small fine with no license consequences,d:License suspension only if later convicted of DUI
note: North Dakota's implied consent law means driving on state roads implies your consent to chemical testing. A first-offense refusal results in a 180-day administrative license suspension plus the refusal can be used as evidence in your DUI case.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: In North Dakota, when must you use your headlights?
options: a:Only between midnight and 5 AM,b:From 30 minutes after sunset to 30 minutes before sunrise and when visibility is under 500 feet,c:Only in rain or snow,d:Only when other vehicles have their lights on
note: North Dakota requires headlights from 30 minutes after sunset to 30 minutes before sunrise and whenever visibility is reduced to less than 500 feet due to weather. North Dakota's blizzards, freezing fog, and blowing snow make headlight use critical for visibility — use them whenever there is any doubt.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: You are approaching a railroad crossing on a North Dakota rural road. The warning lights are flashing. What must you do?
options: a:Slow to 15 mph and proceed if no train is visible,b:Stop before the gate and wait until it fully rises and lights stop before crossing,c:Proceed quickly to beat the train if it appears far away,d:Honk and proceed if you can see the train is not close
note: When railroad crossing warning lights are flashing in North Dakota, stop before the gate or stop line. Wait until the gate rises completely and the lights stop flashing before crossing. Never race a train — trains move faster than they appear and cannot stop quickly.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What is the minimum following distance recommended on North Dakota highways?
options: a:1 second,b:2 seconds,c:3 seconds,d:4 seconds
note: North Dakota recommends a minimum 3-second following distance. On snow and ice — extremely common in North Dakota — increase to at least 8–10 seconds because stopping distances increase dramatically on slippery surfaces.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: You are driving in North Dakota and see an orange sign reading 'Flagger Ahead.' What does this mean?
options: a:A sporting event is nearby — expect pedestrian traffic,b:A road worker is ahead directing traffic — prepare to stop and follow their signals,c:A flag sale is occurring nearby,d:Wind conditions are being monitored — reduce speed to 45 mph
note: An orange 'Flagger Ahead' sign in a North Dakota construction zone means a road worker is controlling traffic with a flag or sign. Prepare to stop. Follow the flagger's directions — they have the authority to control traffic and override traffic signals in construction zones.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When driving on a North Dakota highway and approaching a hill crest or curve, passing is prohibited because:
options: a:Speed limits are lower near hills and curves,b:You cannot see far enough ahead to safely complete a passing maneuver,c:The road surface is always worse near curves,d:Passing is prohibited only when the speed limit exceeds 55 mph
note: You must have adequate sight distance to pass safely — typically at least 1,000 feet on North Dakota highways. Near hill crests and curves, you cannot see far enough to know whether oncoming traffic is approaching. These are always marked as no-passing zones.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What is required before making a lane change on a North Dakota highway?
options: a:Signal, then immediately move to the next lane,b:Signal, check mirrors, check blind spot, and then change lanes when safe,c:Honk your horn to warn other drivers,d:Flash your headlights to signal your intention
note: A safe lane change requires: signal to announce your intention, check all mirrors for approaching traffic, physically check your blind spot by turning your head, and only then change lanes when it is clear. On North Dakota's high-speed highways, this sequence is critical.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: You are driving behind a wide load vehicle (e.g., farm equipment) on a North Dakota highway. What should you expect?
options: a:The vehicle will always pull over to let you pass,b:The vehicle may take up more than one lane — follow at a safe distance and only pass when completely safe,c:Wide load vehicles must always use designated truck routes,d:You may pass wide loads anywhere — they must yield to all traffic
note: North Dakota's rural roads regularly see wide agricultural machinery that may span more than one lane. Follow at a greater distance than normal, never attempt to pass on a curve or hill, and only pass when you have a clear, straight road with adequate sight distance. Watch for escort vehicles with amber lights.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: In North Dakota, where may you NOT make a U-turn?
options: a:On a straight road with good visibility in both directions,b:At an intersection where it is not prohibited by signs,c:At the crest of a hill, on a curve, or where visibility is limited,d:On a county road with no traffic
note: U-turns are prohibited in North Dakota where visibility is limited — at the crest of a hill, on a curve, or anywhere you cannot see at least 500 feet in both directions. They are also prohibited at railroad crossings and in front of fire stations.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Under North Dakota GDL rules, minor drivers under 16 with a restricted Class D license are prohibited from driving during which nighttime hours?
options: a:Between the later of sunset or 9:00 p.m. and 5:00 a.m.,b:Between 11:00 p.m. and 5:00 a.m.,c:Between 10:00 p.m. and 6:00 a.m.,d:Between midnight and 5:00 a.m.
note: In North Dakota, 15-year-old restricted license holders cannot drive unsupervised between the later of sunset or 9:00 p.m. and 5:00 a.m. Exceptions apply for driving to and from work, official school activities, or religious activities.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What is the correct action when you see a yield sign in North Dakota?
options: a:Stop completely regardless of traffic conditions,b:Slow down and give the right of way to all approaching traffic — stop if necessary,c:Maintain your speed — cross traffic must yield to you,d:Yield only to vehicles approaching from your right
note: A yield sign requires you to slow down and give the right of way to all approaching traffic. Stop if necessary. Only proceed when there is a safe gap. Yield signs are used at on-ramps, roundabouts, and intersections where one road crosses another without full stop control.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When parking on a North Dakota street and leaving your vehicle, what must you do?
options: a:Leave the engine running if the weather is very cold,b:Turn off the engine, set the parking brake, and take your keys,c:Leave the vehicle in drive to prevent rolling,d:No requirements — North Dakota has no parking regulations
note: North Dakota requires drivers to turn off the engine, set the parking brake, and take the keys when leaving a parked vehicle. Leaving a running unattended vehicle (called 'puffing') is not only against North Dakota law in some jurisdictions but also creates a theft risk and idling concerns.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Under North Dakota GDL rules, whose vehicles is a 15-year-old with a restricted Class D license allowed to operate?
options: a:Only vehicles owned by their parent, guardian, grandparent, sibling, aunt, or uncle,b:Only vehicles equipped with dual brakes,c:Any passenger vehicle, regardless of ownership,d:Only vehicles registered in North Dakota
note: A 15-year-old driver with a restricted Class D license in North Dakota is legally restricted to driving vehicles owned by a parent, legal guardian, grandparent, sibling, aunt, or uncle. This restriction is removed when they turn 16 and transition to an unrestricted license.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What does a flashing red traffic signal at a North Dakota intersection mean?
options: a:Proceed without stopping if no traffic is visible,b:Slow down and yield to cross traffic,c:Stop completely, yield to all traffic, then proceed when safe,d:Stop and wait for the signal to turn green
note: A flashing red signal in North Dakota is treated exactly like a stop sign. Come to a complete stop, look in all directions, yield to approaching vehicles and pedestrians, and proceed only when it is safe to do so.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If your vehicle's turn signals fail, what should you use to indicate a turn?
options: a:Hand signals,b:Your horn,c:Headlights,d:Hazard lights
note: If your electrical turn signals are not working, you must use standard hand and arm signals to show other drivers when you intend to turn or change lanes. Extend your left arm straight out for a left turn, bend your left arm up at the elbow for a right turn, and bend your left arm down at the elbow to indicate slowing or stopping.

question: Signs indicating public recreation areas are typically what color?
options: a:Green,b:Orange,c:Brown,d:Red
note: Brown traffic signs are used for recreational and cultural interest areas, such as parks, campgrounds, and historic sites. Green signs are generally for directions and distances, orange for temporary work zones, and red for stop or prohibition.

question: If your vehicle's right wheels run off the pavement, what is the safest recovery method?
options: a:Immediately steer sharply back onto the pavement and accelerate.,b:Take your foot off the gas, slow down, steer parallel to the roadway, then gently ease back on when safe.,c:Stop quickly and get out to check damage.
note: If your right wheels leave the pavement, stay calm and avoid jerking the steering wheel. Ease off the accelerator, slow down while keeping the vehicle under control with the wheels parallel to the roadway, then when your speed is reduced and it is safe, gently steer back onto the pavement. Sudden sharp steering or hard braking can cause you to lose control.

question: What does a reflective orange triangle displayed on the rear of a vehicle mean?
options: a:The vehicle often travels at 25 mph or slower.,b:It is an ambulance.,c:It is a school bus.
note: A reflective orange triangle on the rear of a vehicle is the slow-moving vehicle emblem. It warns that the vehicle usually travels at 25 mph or less, such as farm machinery or certain construction or horse-drawn vehicles, so you should be prepared to slow down when approaching.

question: Which factor most affects your ability to stop quickly?
options: a:Time of day.,b:The condition of the road (wet, icy, or dry).,c:Signal lights.
note: Your stopping distance depends heavily on road conditions. Wet, icy, or gravel surfaces greatly reduce traction, increasing the distance needed to stop. On slippery roads you must slow down and increase following distance so you have enough space to stop safely.

question: Drinking coffee after consuming alcohol will do which of the following?
options: a:Has no effect on blood alcohol concentration.,b:Cancels the effect of the alcohol.,c:Decreases blood alcohol concentration.
note: Coffee does not lower your blood alcohol concentration (BAC) or make you sober. It may make you feel more awake, but the alcohol remains in your system until your body has time to process it. Only time reduces BAC.

question: Two solid white lines across a lane indicate what regarding pedestrians?
options: a:Vehicles have right-of-way over pedestrians,b:Pedestrians in crosswalks must be given the right-of-way,c:No one has right-of-way in crosswalks,d:Only bicycles may cross there
note: Two solid white lines across the road mark a crosswalk. Drivers must yield to pedestrians who are in or entering the crosswalk, giving them the right-of-way when they are crossing legally.

question: When using a roundabout, drivers should do which of the following?
options: a:Yield to traffic already in the roundabout,b:Stop within the roundabout,c:Drive clockwise around the central island,d:Enter without signaling
note: Traffic in a roundabout moves counterclockwise, and drivers entering must yield to vehicles already in the circle. You should slow down, yield to circulating traffic and pedestrians, and then enter when it is safe without stopping inside the roundabout unless traffic conditions require it.

question: At dusk or during heavy overcast, which vehicle lights should you use?
options: a:Parking lights.,b:Headlights (low beam).,c:Four-way flashers.
note: At dusk, in heavy overcast, or any time visibility is reduced, you should use your low-beam headlights so other drivers can see you. Parking lights alone are not enough while driving, and four-way flashers are for stopped or emergency situations, not normal driving.

question: What can happen to a bicyclist who fails to obey traffic laws?
options: a:They are exempt from traffic laws.,b:They may be ticketed.,c:They will always receive a warning first.
note: Bicyclists must follow the same basic traffic laws as drivers, such as stopping at stop signs and obeying signals. If they break these laws, they can be stopped and ticketed just like motorists.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At a yield sign you should:
options: a:Always stop before entering the intersection.,b:Yield the right-of-way to traffic in the road you are entering.,c:Yield only to traffic on the right.
note: At a yield sign you are not required to stop every time. You must slow down, be prepared to stop, and let any traffic or pedestrians already in or close to the intersection go first. Stop only if needed to avoid interfering with them.

question: What do crossbuck signs indicate?
options: a:School zones.,b:Railroad crossings.,c:No passing zones.
note: A crossbuck is the white X-shaped sign found at railroad crossings. It marks the location of the tracks and means you must yield to any approaching train, looking and listening carefully before crossing.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If two drivers arrive at the same time to an uncontrolled intersection, who has the right-of-way?
options: a:The driver on the right has the right-of-way.,b:The driver on the left has the right-of-way.,c:One driver may continue driving without stopping.
note: At an uncontrolled intersection where two vehicles arrive at the same time, the driver on the left must yield to the driver on the right. The vehicle on the right has the right-of-way and may proceed first when it is safe.

question: If a transit vehicle is signaling to re-enter traffic after a stop, what must you do?
options: a:Honking to alert the driver.,b:Yield so it can safely re-enter.,c:Speed up to pass before it returns to traffic.
note: When a bus or transit vehicle signals that it is pulling out from a stop, you should yield and allow it to re-enter traffic safely. Slow down or change lanes if needed so the bus can merge without danger.

question: When making a turn, you should do what with your speed?
options: a:Maintain your speed,b:Increase your speed,c:Reduce your speed,d:Vary your speed
note: Before and during a turn, you should reduce your speed to a safe level so you can stay in your lane, maintain control, and react to hazards such as pedestrians, cyclists, or oncoming traffic.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: A red flashing traffic signal is equivalent to which traffic control device?
options: a:A solid red light.,b:A stop sign.,c:A yield sign.
note: A flashing red light means the same as a stop sign: you must come to a complete stop, yield to any traffic or pedestrians with the right-of-way, and proceed only when it is safe.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Compared to smaller vehicles, larger vehicles generally have:
options: a:Smaller blind spots.,b:No blind spots.,c:Larger blind spots.
note: Large vehicles like trucks and buses have bigger blind spots on all sides than passenger cars. Because of these larger no-zones, you should avoid lingering beside them and give them extra space.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: To pass a slower vehicle on a two-lane, two-way road, what is required?
options: a:Never cross the centerline.,b:Use the lane belonging to oncoming traffic when it is safe and legal to do so.,c:Use the shoulder at any time.
note: On a two-lane, two-way road, you must move into the lane used by oncoming traffic to pass, but only where passing is allowed and only when you have enough clear distance to do so safely without exceeding the speed limit.

question: What helps you avoid needing to make emergency stops in traffic?
options: a:Honk your horn to make others aware of you.,b:Look ahead and maintain a safe following distance.,c:Drive only in the right lane.
note: By looking well ahead and keeping a safe following distance, you can see problems early and slow down gradually, which helps you avoid sudden, emergency stops.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What do speed limit signs indicate?
options: a:The maximum or minimum speed legally allowed,b:Potential driving speeds for the area,c:The speed to use in heavy traffic,d:Recommended speed under adverse conditions
note: Speed limit signs show the maximum (and sometimes minimum) legal speed under ideal conditions. You must slow down below the posted limit whenever road, traffic, or weather conditions make the posted speed unsafe.

question: What is the single most effective action to reduce your chance of death or serious injury in a crash?
options: a:Limit your driving to weekdays.,b:Stay in the right lane on multilane highways.,c:Wear your seat belt.
note: Wearing a seat belt greatly reduces your risk of being killed or seriously hurt in a crash by keeping you inside the vehicle, spreading crash forces over stronger parts of your body, and working with airbags. It is the single most effective safety action you can take every time you drive.

question: If you are following a school bus or a tank truck carrying flammable liquids, what should you be prepared to do?
options: a:Decrease your following distance.,b:Pass them on the right.,c:Be prepared to stop at all railroad crossings.
note: School buses and many tank trucks carrying flammable or hazardous materials must stop at all railroad crossings, even if no train is coming. When you follow these vehicles, you should slow down and be ready to stop behind them at the tracks.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When turning left from a multilane, one-way street onto another one-way street, where should you start your turn?
options: a:The right lane.,b:The left lane.,c:The middle of the intersection.
note: On a one‑way street, a left turn should start from the leftmost lane that is lawfully available. When turning onto another one‑way street, you normally turn into the leftmost lane of the new street, unless signs or lane markings direct otherwise.

question: In which situation is it appropriate to sound your horn?
options: a:When you have lost control of your car to alert others.,b:When passing another car on a multilane highway.,c:When you are approaching a green light.
note: Use your horn only to warn others of a hazard, such as when you lose control or another driver is about to hit you. Do not use the horn just to signal routine moves like passing on a multilane road or approaching a green light.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If a crossing guard is directing traffic in a school zone, you must:
options: a:Follow the crossing guard's directions,b:Follow what other drivers are doing instead of the guard,c:Assume the guard has no authority,d:Proceed only on green signal lights
note: Crossing guards have legal authority to direct traffic in school zones. You must follow their instructions, even if traffic signals or other drivers are doing something different, and proceed carefully as they indicate.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At an uncontrolled intersection where you and another vehicle arrive at the same time and the other vehicle is on your right, what should you do?
options: a:Drive into the intersection and make the other vehicle stop.,b:Speed up and get through the intersection.,c:Slow down and yield to the vehicle on your right.
note: At an uncontrolled intersection, if two vehicles arrive at the same time, the driver on the left must yield to the driver on the right. Slowing down and yielding to the vehicle on your right helps prevent collisions and keeps traffic moving safely.

question: The effect of being very tired on your driving ability is similar to which substance's effect?
options: a:Anger.,b:Amphetamines.,c:Alcohol.
note: Severe fatigue affects driving much like alcohol: it slows reaction time, reduces attention, impairs judgment, and can even cause you to fall asleep at the wheel. Driving while very tired can be just as dangerous as driving after drinking.

question: When preparing to change lanes you should:
options: a:Check your side view mirror,b:Check your rearview mirror,c:Quickly glance over your shoulder to check for vehicles,d:Do all of the above
note: Before changing lanes, you must check your mirrors and your blind spot. Use your rearview and side mirrors to see traffic behind and beside you, then quickly glance over your shoulder to check the blind spot that mirrors cannot show. Doing all of these steps helps ensure the lane is clear.

question: When driving in fog, which of the following should you do?
options: a:Use high beam headlights,b:Drive cautiously and reduce your speed,c:Use parking lights only,d:Speed up to clear the fog quickly
note: In fog, visibility is reduced, so you should slow down and drive cautiously. Use low beam headlights, because high beams reflect off the fog and make it harder to see. Never speed up to get through fog; you may not see hazards in time to stop.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: After passing another vehicle on a two-lane road with traffic in opposite directions, when should you return to your lane?
options: a:Return to the driving lane when there's enough room between you and the vehicle you passed.,b:Remain in the left lane if you intend to turn left.,c:Return to the right side of the roadway immediately.
note: After passing on a two-lane road, you should not move back into your lane until there is plenty of space between you and the vehicle you passed. A good rule is to wait until you can see the front of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror, which indicates you have enough room to return safely.

question: What does a double solid yellow centerline on a two-lane road indicate?
options: a:Lanes are moving in the same direction and drivers are not permitted to pass.,b:Lanes are moving in opposite directions and drivers are permitted to pass when it is safe to do so.,c:Lanes are moving in opposite directions and drivers are not permitted to pass.
note: A double solid yellow centerline means traffic in the two lanes is moving in opposite directions and neither side is allowed to cross the lines to pass. Yellow always separates opposite directions; solid means no passing.

question: How can you prevent drowsiness on long trips?
options: a:Stop at regular intervals to rest and stretch.,b:Turn on your car radio loud.,c:Slow down and drive more slowly than traffic.
note: To prevent drowsiness on long trips, you should plan regular stops to get out, walk, and stretch. Short breaks help you stay alert much better than turning up the radio or just slowing down, which do not actually reduce fatigue.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: From a center lane reserved for turning, which maneuver(s) are permitted?
options: a:You may make left turns from either direction.,b:You may pass slow-moving traffic using the lane.,c:You may drive straight through the intersection from the center lane.
note: A center left‑turn lane is only for making left turns from either direction, or for beginning and ending a left‑turn maneuver. It must not be used to pass other vehicles or to continue straight through an intersection.

question: Which is a safe method to drive through a curve?
options: a:Speed up as you enter and slow as you exit,b:Slow down before entering the curve and gradually accelerate on exit,c:Maintain constant speed throughout the curve,d:Brake sharply in the middle of the curve
note: For safe curve driving, slow down before you enter the curve so the car is stable, then gently accelerate as you exit. Braking hard or changing speed sharply in the middle of the curve can cause loss of traction.

question: What does a solid white line down the center of a two-lane road indicate?
options: a:Lanes are moving in opposite directions and drivers are not permitted to pass.,b:Lanes are moving in opposite directions and drivers may pass when safe.,c:Lanes are moving in the same direction and drivers are not permitted to pass.
note: White lines separate traffic moving in the same direction. A solid white line between lanes means lane changes are discouraged or sometimes prohibited, so you should generally stay in your lane and not pass across it.

question: You see the driver ahead using one hand and talking to a passenger. What should you do?
options: a:Give the vehicle extra space,b:Ignore and follow closely,c:Copy their behavior,d:Flash your lights to warn them
note: If you notice another driver is distracted, increase your following distance and give them extra space. Distracted drivers are more likely to make sudden or unpredictable moves, so staying farther back gives you more time to react and helps prevent collisions.

question: How are bicycles treated on the roadway under traffic laws?
options: a:They must always yield to motor vehicles.,b:They do not follow specific rules of the road.,c:They are considered vehicles with the same rights and responsibilities as motor vehicles.
note: Bicycles are generally treated as vehicles on the road. Cyclists must obey traffic signals, signs, lane markings, and right‑of‑way rules just like drivers of motor vehicles, and they are entitled to use the roadway and be given the same respect and space as other vehicles.

question: When driving past a vehicle that has just parked at the curb, what assumption should you make?
options: a:That the parked driver will open their car door as you approach.,b:That the parked driver will wait for you.,c:That you can speed up past them safely.
note: When passing a parked vehicle, assume someone inside may suddenly open a door or pull out without warning. Slow down if needed and leave as much space as safely possible so you have room to react if a door opens or the vehicle moves.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When parking uphill on a street with a curb, how should you turn your front wheels?
options: a:Turn your front wheels sharply toward the curb.,b:Turn your front wheels sharply away from the curb.,c:Turn your front wheels slightly to the right.
note: When parking uphill with a curb, turn your front wheels sharply away from the curb and set the parking brake. If the vehicle rolls, the back of the front tire will rest against the curb, stopping the car from rolling into traffic.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At an uncontrolled intersection with no signs or signals, which vehicle has the right-of-way when two vehicles arrive at the same time?
options: a:The vehicle approaching from the right,b:The vehicle approaching from the left,c:The vehicle that honks first,d:The vehicle which is larger
note: At an uncontrolled intersection where two vehicles arrive at the same time, the driver must yield to the vehicle on their right. This rule helps decide who goes first when there are no signs or signals, reducing confusion and preventing collisions.

question: If you're driving in another driver's blind spot, what should you do?
options: a:Hold your position until they change lanes,b:Move forward or fall back so the other driver can see you,c:Stay in their blind spot to prevent them from merging,d:Flash your lights repeatedly
note: Avoid driving in another driver’s blind spot because they may not see you if they change lanes or turn. Either speed up to move ahead where you are visible in their mirrors, or slow down to fall back so you can clearly see their face in the side mirror. This gives both you and the other driver more time and space to react safely.

question: What do large flashing arrow panels in a work or lane-closure area tell drivers to do?
options: a:Drivers may stay in their current lane.,b:There is something to view in direction of the arrow.,c:Merge out of the closed lane in the direction indicated by the arrow.
note: Large flashing or sequential arrow panels in work zones warn that a lane is closed ahead and direct you to move out of that lane. You should slow down, be prepared for workers and equipment, and merge safely in the direction the arrow points. Do not wait until the last moment to merge, as that increases the risk of crashes.

question: When driving near heavy trucks, other drivers must allow for what truck characteristic?
options: a:The increased stopping distance required by large vehicles.,b:The decreased stopping distance required by large vehicles.,c:The decreased noise of larger vehicles.
note: Heavy trucks are much heavier than passenger cars and need a longer distance to stop, especially at higher speeds or in bad weather. When driving near trucks, avoid cutting in front of them, give them extra space, and remember they may not be able to stop as quickly as you can.

question: Which of these actions helps reduce road rage and aggressive driving?
options: a:Using proper turn signals and obeying speed limits.,b:Allowing extra travel time.,c:All of the above.
note: Using turn signals, obeying speed limits, and allowing extra travel time all help reduce stress and prevent aggressive driving. When you plan ahead and drive courteously, you are less likely to feel rushed or frustrated, and other drivers are less likely to react angrily to your actions.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: A sign that reads 'Reduced speed, 35 mph' means what?
options: a:The new 35 mph limit begins at that sign,b:You may slow at your convenience later,c:The sign is only advisory and not enforceable,d:The reduced limit starts at the next speed sign
note: A regulatory speed limit sign, including one that says something like “Reduced speed 35 mph,” means the posted speed becomes the legal maximum at that sign unless another sign indicates a different point. You must slow down to at or below that speed by the time you reach the sign, not sometime later.

question: If you find a vehicle defect that could affect safety, you should:
options: a:Correct it as soon as possible,b:Wait until you can afford repairs,c:Drive more slowly and ignore it,d:Cover it up and drive on
note: Any defect that could affect the safe operation of your vehicle should be repaired as soon as possible, ideally before you drive again. Driving with known safety defects increases the risk of a breakdown or crash and can make you legally responsible if a collision occurs.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Two solid yellow lines down the center of the road mean:
options: a:Passing is allowed for drivers from both directions.,b:Passing is not allowed.,c:You may pass if you are at the top of a hill.
note: Two solid yellow lines in the center of the road mean you may not pass from either direction. You can cross them only to turn left into or out of a driveway or side road, or when specifically allowed by signs, but not to pass another moving vehicle.

question: What is 'highway hypnosis' caused by?
options: a:Staring at the roadway for long periods without actively scanning,b:Frequent rest stops,c:Too much sleep before a trip,d:Driving with a passenger
note: Highway hypnosis happens when you stare straight ahead for long periods and stop actively scanning mirrors, instruments, and the road environment. Your mind drifts, and you may not notice hazards. Taking regular breaks, moving your eyes, and staying mentally engaged with the driving task help prevent it.

question: A useful rule for passing is to:
options: a:Pass on the right whenever possible,b:Drive with the flow of traffic and pass only when necessary,c:Always try to get to the front of slow traffic,d:Pass multiple vehicles at once to reduce time spent passing
note: Safe drivers travel with the flow of traffic within the speed limit and pass only when it is truly necessary and clearly safe. Passing always carries extra risk because you move into oncoming or faster traffic, so you should avoid unnecessary passing and never exceed the speed limit to pass.

question: What does a diamond-shaped traffic sign warn drivers about?
options: a:Warns of existing or possible hazards.,b:Alerts drivers to school zones.,c:Alerts drivers to public recreation areas.
note: Diamond-shaped signs are warning signs. They alert you to existing or possible hazards such as curves, intersections, merging traffic, or work zones. They are usually yellow for general warnings or orange in construction and maintenance areas.

question: Fluorescent yellow-green signs are used to warn drivers about what?
options: a:School zones, pedestrian, and bicycle crossings.,b:Hospital locations.,c:Speed limits only.
note: Fluorescent yellow‑green signs are reserved for high‑priority warning situations involving people on foot or on bikes, especially around schools. When you see this color, expect school zones, school crossings, pedestrian crossings, or bicycle crossings and be prepared to slow down and watch carefully.

question: You are in the left lane and want to move into the right lane. What checks should you make before changing lanes?
options: a:Check mirrors, signal, and look over your left shoulder.,b:Check your mirrors, signal, and look over your right shoulder for traffic in the blind spot.,c:Check mirrors only and then change lanes.
note: Before changing lanes to the right, check your mirrors, signal, and then quickly look over your right shoulder to check your blind spot. Mirrors alone do not show vehicles in the blind spot, so the shoulder check is essential to avoid sideswiping another vehicle or a motorcycle.

question: On slippery roads, what is the best action to take?
options: a:Drive the posted speed limit, with caution.,b:Drive more quickly.,c:Slow down.
note: On slippery roads, your tires have less grip, so it takes longer to stop and is easier to skid. You should slow down and increase your following distance so you have more time and space to brake and steer smoothly without losing control.

question: When approaching a steady yellow traffic light, drivers should:
options: a:Accelerate to beat the red,b:Slow to a stop unless already in the intersection,c:Ignore it and proceed at the same speed,d:Back up if possible
note: A steady yellow light means the signal is about to turn red. You must stop before the intersection if you can do so safely. If you are already in the intersection or too close to stop safely when it turns yellow, continue through with caution instead of accelerating.

question: If you stop at a railroad crossing that has more than one track, when should you proceed?
options: a:Go through as soon as the first train passes.,b:Wait until you have a clear view of all tracks.,c:Stop on the first track and watch for another train.
note: At a crossing with more than one track, a second train can come from either direction after the first one passes. Stay stopped until the first train is completely gone and you have a clear view down all tracks in both directions, then proceed only when you are sure no other train is coming.

question: Which greatly increases stopping distances and crash severity?
options: a:High speeds,b:Slow speeds,c:Night driving,d:Smooth tires
note: Higher speeds make it take much longer to stop because your vehicle travels farther during reaction and braking. They also greatly increase the force of a crash, so collisions are more severe at higher speeds.

question: When dealing with pedestrians, a driver must:
options: a:Yield the right-of-way to all pedestrians regardless of where they are crossing,b:Only yield to pedestrians who are legally entitled to it,c:Make sure the pedestrian always signals before crossing,d:Demand the pedestrian wait until the vehicle has passed
note: Drivers must always try to avoid hitting pedestrians and must yield the right‑of‑way to pedestrians who are crossing legally in crosswalks or as traffic signals direct. Even when a pedestrian is crossing illegally, you must slow or stop if needed to avoid a collision, but the legal right‑of‑way is not automatic in every situation.

question: Where are stop lines painted on the roadway?
options: a:In curves and on hills.,b:Next to churches and schools.,c:At intersections and pedestrian crosswalks.
note: A stop line is a solid white line painted across the lane at an intersection or before a crosswalk. You must stop with your front bumper just before this line so pedestrians and cross traffic are protected.

question: If there is an oncoming car to your left and a bicyclist to your right, how should you handle passing the bicyclist?
options: a:Pull onto the shoulder between them.,b:Split the difference and squeeze through.,c:Let the oncoming car pass, then pass the bicyclist when it is safe.
note: When you have hazards on both sides, deal with them one at a time. Slow down and let the oncoming car pass first, then move over and pass the bicyclist with plenty of space when it is safe.

question: If you come to a roadway that is covered with water, what should you do?
options: a:Drive until you think the water is too deep.,b:Turn around and find another way to go.,c:Drive through, as it is unlikely the standing water will become too deep.
note: Never drive into water covering the road because you cannot judge its depth or the strength of the current, and the road surface may be washed out. Turn around and use another route.

question: Regulatory traffic signs are usually what color and must be obeyed?
options: a:Blue.,b:White.,c:Green.
note: Regulatory signs tell you what you must or must not do, such as speed limits, no parking, or one-way directions. In the U.S., these signs are typically white with black or red lettering or symbols, and they are legally enforceable, so you must obey them.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When may you go through an intersection controlled by a stop sign that has no stop line or crosswalk?
options: a:After slowing down to verify that there is no cross traffic.,b:After you come to a complete stop and verify it is safe to proceed.,c:After you have stopped at least 20 feet prior to the intersection.
note: At a stop sign with no stop line or crosswalk, you must come to a complete stop before entering the intersection. Stop at the point nearest the intersection where you can clearly see cross traffic, then proceed only when it is safe.

question: Your vehicle's brake lights signal to other drivers that you are:
options: a:Changing lanes.,b:Slowing down or stopping.,c:Making a turn.
note: Brake lights warn drivers behind you that you are slowing down or stopping. Keeping your brake lights working properly gives others time to react and helps prevent rear-end collisions.

question: How should you regard railroad crossings in terms of safety?
options: a:Generally safe to cross without checking.,b:Always potentially dangerous—look and listen for trains.,c:Safe places to park if you need to stop.
note: Railroad crossings are always potentially dangerous because trains cannot stop quickly and always have the right of way. Slow down, look and listen for trains, and obey all warning signs, signals, and gates before crossing the tracks.

question: Approaching a stopped school bus with its stop arm extended, what must you do?
options: a:Come to a complete stop and wait until the stop arm is withdrawn.,b:Honk your horn before passing the bus on its left.,c:Continue driving when you think most kids have exited.
note: When a school bus is stopped with its red lights flashing and stop arm extended, you must stop your vehicle and remain stopped until the lights stop flashing and the stop arm is withdrawn, unless you are on the opposite side of a divided highway where state law provides an exception.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When making a left turn, to whom must you yield the right-of-way?
options: a:Pedestrians who are already in the intersection.,b:Oncoming traffic.,c:Other drivers who are already in the intersection.
note: When turning left you must yield to oncoming traffic. You must also yield to pedestrians, bicyclists, and any drivers already in the intersection.

question: Which of the following best describes alcohol's effect on driving skills?
options: a:Only a blood alcohol level greater than the legal limit can limit driving ability.,b:Alcohol does not affect driving abilities.,c:Even the smallest amount of alcohol can reduce concentration, perception, judgment, and memory.
note: Even small amounts of alcohol can slow your reactions and interfere with your ability to judge speed, distance, and traffic situations. It reduces concentration, perception, judgment, and memory, which are all critical for safe driving. Because of this, there is no amount of alcohol that is truly safe when you are behind the wheel.

question: If you stop along the road at night, what lighting should you use?
options: a:Turn off all your lights.,b:Leave your low beam headlights on and use emergency flashers.,c:Use parking lights only.
note: If you must stop along the road at night, you want your vehicle to be as visible as possible to approaching drivers. Keep your low beam headlights on so you do not blind others, and turn on your emergency flashers to warn traffic that your vehicle is stopped. This combination helps prevent rear-end and side-swipe collisions.

question: If the centerline shows a broken yellow line next to a solid yellow line, what does that mean?
options: a:Passing is permitted from either direction.,b:Passing is permitted from the lane next to the broken line.,c:Passing is permitted from the lane next to the solid line.
note: A broken yellow line next to a solid yellow line separates traffic moving in opposite directions. Vehicles traveling in the lane next to the broken line may cross it to pass when it is safe. Vehicles traveling next to the solid line must not cross it to pass. This pattern tells you which direction is allowed to pass.

question: If your accelerator becomes stuck while driving, what should you do first?
options: a:Reach down and attempt to pull it up.,b:Shift to neutral and apply steady pressure on the brake.,c:Shift to park immediately.
note: If your accelerator sticks, keep your eyes on the road, shift the transmission to neutral, and apply steady, firm pressure on the brake. Shifting to neutral disconnects the engine power from the wheels so the car stops accelerating, while braking brings the vehicle under control. Once you have slowed, move to the side of the road and stop in a safe place. Do not reach down to pull up the pedal while moving, and do not shift to park until the vehicle is fully stopped.

question: When approaching a railroad crossing with no signals, what is the correct precaution?
options: a:Always bring the car to a complete stop.,b:All railroad crossings have signals so you will never encounter this situation.,c:Slow down and be prepared to stop if a train is approaching.
note: At a railroad crossing without signals or gates, you must slow down, look and listen for trains in both directions, and be ready to stop. You are not required to stop every time if no train is approaching, but you must never assume the tracks are clear.

question: When you see a railroad crossing warning sign, what should you be prepared to do?
options: a:Look for a way around any lowered gates.,b:Be prepared to stop if a train is nearby.,c:Be ready to drive faster than the train.
note: A railroad crossing warning sign means you are approaching tracks and must be ready to slow or stop if a train is near. Look and listen for trains, obey any signals or gates, and never drive around lowered gates.

question: Work zone signs indicate what about driving conditions?
options: a:It is summer.,b:You must immediately stop and back up.,c:Less-than-ideal driving conditions are ahead; use caution.
note: Work zone signs warn that road or traffic conditions may change ahead due to construction, workers, or equipment. You should slow down, be alert for lane shifts or stopped traffic, and follow posted work zone speed limits.

question: What does a solid yellow arrow displayed as part of a traffic signal indicate?
options: a:Is never used as a traffic signal.,b:It has the same meaning as a circular yellow light; prepare to stop.,c:Means drivers may always turn in the arrow's direction without caution.
note: A solid yellow arrow means the protected turning movement is ending. It has the same meaning as a circular yellow light: the signal is about to turn red, so you should slow down and prepare to stop unless you are too close to the intersection to stop safely.

question: If a flagger is directing traffic in a construction zone, what must you do?
options: a:Assume the flagger is not supposed to be directing traffic.,b:Follow the directions given by the flagger.,c:Copy what surrounding traffic is doing regardless of the flagger's instructions.
note: In construction zones, you must obey the directions of a flagger, as their instructions override traffic signals and signs when present. Follow their signals, slow down, and proceed carefully to protect workers and other drivers.

question: What is a good practice to help avoid fatigue on a long trip?
options: a:Stop and rest every two hours.,b:Drive with one eye open at a time.,c:Do arm exercises every hour.
note: Stopping to rest about every two hours is a standard safety practice on long trips. Short breaks help reduce fatigue, keep you alert, and give you a chance to stretch, hydrate, and refocus. If you start to feel drowsy, you should pull over in a safe place and rest rather than trying to push through.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: You must not drive faster than which of the following?
options: a:The posted maximum speed limit only.,b:A speed that is faster than is reasonable and prudent for conditions.,c:Only a speed that is safe for existing conditions.
note: You must never drive faster than is reasonable and prudent for current conditions, even if that speed is below the posted limit. The basic speed law requires you to adjust your speed for traffic, weather, visibility, and road conditions. The posted speed limit is the maximum under ideal conditions, not a guaranteed safe speed in all situations.

question: When you approach a flashing yellow light, you should:
options: a:Increase your speed,b:Come to a complete stop,c:Slow down and proceed with caution,d:Turn off your headlights
note: A flashing yellow light means proceed with caution. You should slow down, look carefully for cross traffic, pedestrians, or other hazards, and continue through the intersection only when it is safe. You are not required to stop unless needed for safety.

question: How does alcohol affect your reflexes and judgment?
options: a:The effect depends on whether it is beer or wine,b:Any type of alcohol impairs reflexes and judgment,c:Only mixed drinks have a strong effect,d:Hard ciders are most impairing
note: Any alcoholic beverage—beer, wine, or liquor—contains ethanol, which slows your brain and nervous system. This reduces your reflexes, coordination, and judgment, making it harder to react quickly and make safe driving decisions. The main factor is how much alcohol you consume, not the type of drink.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Unless otherwise posted, what is the maximum speed limit in a business or residential district?
options: a:55 mph,b:40 mph,c:25 mph,d:35 mph
note: In many states, the default maximum speed limit in business and residential districts is 25 mph when no other limit is posted. This lower speed helps protect pedestrians, cyclists, and drivers in areas with driveways, intersections, and frequent turning movements.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When is driving below the posted speed limit illegal?
options: a:Only when in heavy traffic.,b:When driving slowly disrupts the normal flow of traffic.,c:Only when driving in rural areas.
note: Driving below the posted speed limit becomes illegal when you are going so slowly that you interfere with the normal, safe flow of traffic. You must adjust your speed to conditions, but you cannot drive unreasonably slowly and create a hazard or blockage for other road users.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you miss your exit on an interstate expressway, what is the safe procedure?
options: a:Stop and make a U-turn on the highway.,b:Get off at the next exit and return to the missed exit.,c:Roll down your window and ask the driver next to you for directions.
note: If you miss your exit on an interstate, you must never stop, back up, or make a U‑turn on the highway. Continue to the next exit, leave the freeway safely, and then re-enter in the opposite direction or follow signs to return to your intended exit.

question: Many crashes are caused by drivers doing which of the following?
options: a:Driving too fast for conditions,b:Consistently checking mirrors and blind spots,c:Yielding the right-of-way often,d:Using turn signals too much
note: A major cause of crashes is driving too fast for conditions, even if you are below the posted speed limit. Rain, fog, traffic, curves, and poor visibility all require you to slow down so you can stop safely and maintain control of your vehicle.

question: When is parking or stopping on the shoulder of a freeway permitted?
options: a:If no part of your vehicle is on the road.,b:Only in an emergency.,c:As long as you turn on your four-way (emergency) flashers.
note: On freeways, stopping or parking on the shoulder is generally prohibited except for emergencies such as breakdowns or medical issues. If you must stop, pull as far onto the shoulder as safely possible, turn on your hazard flashers, and stay aware of fast-moving traffic.

question: When approaching a roundabout, you should always do what?
options: a:Increase your speed,b:Slow down before entering,c:Come to a complete stop at the yield line every time,d:Signal left as you enter
note: When approaching a roundabout, you should slow down and be prepared to yield to traffic already in the circle and to pedestrians in crosswalks. Enter at a safe, low speed, then proceed counterclockwise and signal when you exit.

question: What should be your first response to reduced visibility?
options: a:Turn on your headlights,b:Reduce your speed,c:Turn on windshield wipers,d:Pull off the road immediately
note: When visibility decreases due to fog, heavy rain, snow, or darkness, your first and most important response is to reduce your speed so you have more time to see and react to hazards. Headlights and wipers help you see and be seen, but slowing down is what most directly increases your safety margin.

question: If you hear a siren behind you while driving, what action must you take?
options: a:Speed up to get out of the way.,b:Stop where you are.,c:Pull over to the right and stop to allow the emergency vehicle to pass.
note: When an emergency vehicle approaches with its siren on and/or lights flashing, you must safely pull over to the right side of the road and stop, allowing it a clear path. Do not speed up or stop in the lane; staying put in the lane can block the vehicle and speeding up can create more danger.

question: If you're driving so slowly that traffic is backing up behind you, what should you do?
options: a:Increase your speed to match traffic,b:Pull off the right side of the road and let traffic pass,c:Not let other cars pass you,d:Stop in the travel lane
note: If your slow driving is causing a line of vehicles to form behind you, you should safely pull onto the right shoulder or into a turnout where allowed and let the traffic pass. This is especially important on two-lane roads where others cannot easily pass. Do not block traffic or speed beyond a safe speed just to keep up.

question: When must you stop for a school bus?
options: a:When it approaches you, even if its lights are not flashing.,b:That is parked on the shoulder of the road with no one in it.,c:If you are both driving on a two-lane highway and its red lights are flashing.
note: On a two-lane roadway, traffic in both directions must stop for a stopped school bus with flashing red lights and an extended stop arm while children are boarding or leaving the bus.

question: Alcohol consumption typically causes which impairment?
options: a:Improved concentration,b:Enhanced coordination,c:Loss of concentration and slower judgment,d:Sharper vision
note: Alcohol is a depressant that slows brain and body functions. It reduces concentration, slows judgment and reaction time, and impairs coordination and vision. Even small amounts can affect your ability to make safe driving decisions and respond quickly to hazards.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Who must wear a seat belt under North Dakota law?
options: a:Only the driver,b:All drivers and front-seat occupants; occupants under 18 anywhere in the vehicle must be properly restrained,c:Only passengers in the back seat,d:Only occupants under 18
note: North Dakota law requires the driver and all front-seat occupants to wear seat belts. In addition, all occupants under 18 must be properly restrained in any seat in the vehicle, using a seat belt or appropriate child restraint. This protects younger passengers throughout the vehicle, not just in the front.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What is the typical maximum speed limit on a paved divided highway unless otherwise posted?
options: a:40 mph.,b:55 mph.,c:70 mph.
note: On most rural two-lane and many divided highways, the typical statutory maximum speed limit is 55 mph unless signs show a different limit. Higher limits such as 65 or 70 mph apply only where specifically posted. You must always follow the posted speed limit, even if it is lower than the general maximum.

question: A diamond-shaped sign generally indicates what?
options: a:An interstate route sign,b:A school crossing,c:A road hazard or warning,d:A regulatory instruction
note: Diamond-shaped signs are warning signs. They alert you to hazards or special conditions ahead, such as curves, intersections, pedestrian crossings, or work zones. They are usually yellow, or orange in construction and maintenance areas.

question: Diagonal stripes sloping down to the right on a barricade indicate that drivers should:
options: a:Bear to the left,b:Bear to the right,c:Stop and wait,d:Turn around
note: On barricades and object markers, diagonal stripes show which side you should pass on. If the stripes slope downward to the right, you should bear or pass to the right of the barricade. If they slope downward to the left, you should pass to the left.

question: You are in the right lane on a multilane highway and want to move into the left lane. What should you do before changing lanes?
options: a:Look in your rearview mirror for traffic behind you.,b:Check your mirrors, signal, and look over your left shoulder for traffic in your blind spot before changing lanes.,c:Look in your side mirror only and then change lanes.
note: Before changing lanes, you must check your mirrors, signal, and then quickly look over your shoulder in the direction you are moving to check your blind spot. Mirrors alone cannot show vehicles in your blind spot, so the over-the-shoulder glance is essential for a safe lane change.

question: On which surface does your vehicle's stopping distance increase significantly?
options: a:On paved highways.,b:On a wet or icy road.,c:When driving at night.
note: Stopping distance increases greatly on wet, icy, or loose surfaces because your tires have less traction. On these surfaces you need more space to stop, so slow down and leave extra following distance.

question: If you're involved in a serious crash, what actions should you take?
options: a:Call the police.,b:Stop, check for injuries, provide aid if needed, call 911, move vehicles out of traffic if possible, and report the crash when required.,c:Determine if anyone is injured.
note: After a serious crash, you must stop at the scene, check for injuries, and provide reasonable help, such as calling 911. If possible, move vehicles out of traffic to prevent another collision. You must report the crash to law enforcement when state law requires, especially when there are injuries, deaths, or significant property damage.

question: When another vehicle is approaching from the opposite direction at night, which headlight setting should you use?
options: a:High-beam setting.,b:Low-beam setting.,c:Turn off headlights and use parking lights only.
note: Use low-beam headlights when an oncoming vehicle is approaching so you do not blind the other driver. High beams should only be used when there is no oncoming traffic and you are not closely following another vehicle.

question: North Dakota law requires headlights to be used when?
options: a:Between sunset and sunrise and when visibility is poor,b:Only during rain or snow,c:When the temperature drops below freezing,d:When you are tired
note: Headlights must be used from sunset to sunrise and any time visibility is poor, such as in rain, snow, or fog. You must dim to low beams within about 500 feet of an oncoming vehicle and when following another vehicle closely so you do not blind other drivers.

question: What does a green arrow traffic signal mean for the lane it applies to?
options: a:You may proceed in the direction indicated by the arrow,b:It only applies on one-way streets,c:You may proceed only if a circular green light is also on,d:It means slow down and prepare to stop
note: A green arrow means you have a protected movement in the direction of the arrow. You may proceed in that direction after yielding to any vehicles or pedestrians already in the intersection; oncoming traffic and conflicting movements are stopped by a red light.

question: Under what circumstances may you drive around lowered railroad crossing gates?
options: a:When the train has passed.,b:Under no circumstances.,c:When the lights have stopped flashing.
note: You must never drive around lowered railroad crossing gates. Lowered gates and flashing signals mean a train is approaching or may be approaching, even if you do not see it yet. It is both extremely dangerous and illegal to go around the gates; you must wait until the gates are fully raised and the signals stop before crossing.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What does a steady red traffic light require drivers to do?
options: a:Drive through the intersection if there is no crossing traffic.,b:Stop and come to a complete stop before the crosswalk or stop line.,c:Stop only if a police officer is nearby.
note: A steady red light means you must come to a complete stop before the stop line, crosswalk, or entering the intersection. After stopping, you may turn right (and in some states left from a one‑way to a one‑way) only if there is no sign prohibiting it and the way is clear of traffic and pedestrians. If a sign says NO TURN ON RED, you must remain stopped until the light turns green.

question: When you approach a railroad crossing with signals flashing, what must you do?
options: a:Slow down and look for a train.,b:Stop and look for a train (do not stop closer than 15 feet and no farther than 50 feet from the nearest rail).,c:Look for a train, then speed up across the tracks.
note: When the signals at a railroad crossing are flashing, you must stop and not proceed until the signals stop and it is clearly safe to cross. Federal guidance and many state laws require stopping no closer than 15 feet and no farther than 50 feet from the nearest rail. Stopping in this zone keeps you safely away from the train’s path while still allowing you to see down the tracks.

question: What is the key rule for speed management in curves?
options: a:Slow down before entering the curve,b:Accelerate gently while entering the curve,c:Maintain posted speed through the curve and brake at the apex,d:Speed up before entering to maintain momentum
note: Before entering a curve, you should slow down to a safe speed. Braking is most effective while your vehicle is still traveling straight; once you are in the curve, sudden braking can cause skidding or loss of control. Enter the curve at a reduced speed, then maintain a steady speed through it and accelerate gently as you exit if conditions allow.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What must you do when you encounter a flashing red traffic light at an intersection?
options: a:Slow down and drive carefully through the intersection.,b:Stop at the intersection and then proceed when it is safe.,c:Wait for a flashing green light to proceed.
note: A flashing red light is treated like a stop sign. You must come to a complete stop at the stop line, crosswalk, or before entering the intersection, then proceed only when traffic and pedestrians are clear and it is safe to go.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When should you look over your shoulder to check a blind spot?
options: a:When changing lanes.,b:When pulling toward or away from a curb.,c:Both when changing lanes and when pulling toward or away from a curb.
note: Blind spots are areas you cannot see with your mirrors alone. You must quickly look over your shoulder before changing lanes and when moving toward or away from the curb to be sure no vehicle, bicycle, or pedestrian is in that hidden area.

question: When driving in traffic, what is the safest speed strategy?
options: a:Drive slower than the flow of traffic.,b:Drive with the flow of traffic within the posted speed limit.,c:Fluctuate your speed to keep alert.
note: The safest strategy is to travel with the general flow of traffic while staying at or below the posted speed limit. Driving much faster or much slower than surrounding traffic increases the risk of collisions because other drivers may not anticipate your speed.

question: How should you check blind spots before changing lanes?
options: a:Use the inside rearview mirror only.,b:Use both inside and outside rearview mirrors and glance over your shoulder.,c:Use the outside rearview mirror only.
note: Mirrors alone do not show everything around your vehicle. Before changing lanes, check your inside and outside mirrors and then quickly glance over your shoulder in the direction you plan to move to make sure no one is in your blind spot.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When should you signal before passing another vehicle?
options: a:Signal early enough for other drivers to know your intentions.,b:Signal just before changing lanes.,c:Signal after changing lanes.
note: Turn on your turn signal well before you move into another lane so other drivers, motorcyclists, and bicyclists have time to see your signal and adjust. Signaling only at the last moment or after you move does not give others enough warning.

question: When approaching a heavy truck while driving uphill from behind, what should you expect about the truck's speed?
options: a:The truck may be traveling at a speed slower than the posted speed limit.,b:You may not be able to legally pass the truck.,c:You may not be able to safely pass the truck.
note: Heavy trucks often slow down on uphill grades because of their weight, so they may travel below the posted speed limit. Expect them to be slower, increase your following distance, and only pass if it is legal and you have enough clear distance to do so safely.

question: At a light rail intersection, what should you always do?
options: a:Look both ways before crossing and obey all traffic signals.,b:Share the road only with pedestrians.,c:Assume trams always stop for you.
note: At light rail intersections, you must obey all traffic signals and warning devices and always look both ways for approaching trains. Never drive around lowered gates or ignore flashing lights, because trains cannot stop quickly and always have the right-of-way.

question: If another driver acts aggressively toward you, what should you do?
options: a:Cut them off to slow them down.,b:Retaliate by tailgating them.,c:Avoid eye contact, slow down, and let them pass.
note: When another driver is aggressive, your goal is to avoid a confrontation and reduce risk. Do not respond, make eye contact, or retaliate. Instead, stay calm, slow down, and safely let the aggressive driver pass so you can increase the space between your vehicle and theirs.

question: When parking uphill on a street with a curb, what is the correct wheel position?
options: a:Keep the front wheel straight and set the parking brake.,b:Turn the front wheels away from the curb and set the parking brake.,c:Turn the front wheels toward the curb and set the parking brake.
note: When parking uphill with a curb, turn the front wheels away from the curb and set the parking brake. If the vehicle rolls, the back of the front tire will rest against the curb and stop the car from rolling into traffic.

question: How does driving at night compare to driving during the day?
options: a:Less dangerous.,b:No more or less dangerous.,c:More dangerous.
note: Driving at night is more dangerous because you can see less distance ahead, it is harder to judge speed and position, and glare from headlights can reduce visibility. There are also more fatigued or impaired drivers on the road at night, increasing crash risk.

question: A regulatory sign with a red circle and diagonal slash through a black symbol means:
options: a:That drivers should come to a complete stop.,b:That the depicted action is forbidden.,c:That some drivers should yield to others.
note: A regulatory sign with a red circle and a diagonal slash over a black symbol means the action shown is not allowed. For example, a right-turn arrow with a red circle and slash means no right turn at that location.

question: Why must you exercise extra caution when driving at night?
options: a:There is typically higher traffic volume,b:You cannot see as well in the dark,c:Traffic moves faster at night,d:Roads are more slippery at night
note: Driving at night is more dangerous because you cannot see as far or as clearly as in daylight. Reduced visibility makes it harder to spot hazards, judge distances, and see pedestrians, animals, or objects in the road, so you must use headlights and drive more cautiously.

question: When is it appropriate to use your horn?
options: a:While passing a bicyclist,b:When traveling through an intersection,c:To warn a child who is about to run into the street,d:To greet a friend on the road
note: Use your horn only to help prevent a collision, such as when a child or pedestrian is about to step into the street and may not see you. Avoid using the horn unnecessarily, like to greet friends or out of anger, because it can startle others and create unsafe situations.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: You may pass another vehicle when the line dividing your lane from the lane you wish to enter is what type of line?
options: a:Double solid yellow.,b:Broken white (or a broken line on your side of the center).,c:Solid yellow.
note: You may pass or change lanes when there is a broken line on your side and it is safe to do so. Broken white lines separate lanes moving in the same direction on multi‑lane roads and may be crossed to change lanes. For two‑way roads with yellow center lines, you may pass only when the yellow line on your side is broken, never across a double solid yellow line.

question: Why should you avoid following another vehicle too closely?
options: a:You may not have time to stop if the vehicle in front slows or stops suddenly.,b:You may not see the road between the cars.,c:You may not see the vehicle's turn signals.
note: Following too closely, or tailgating, leaves you too little time and space to react if the vehicle ahead slows or stops suddenly. Keeping a safe following distance gives you enough room to brake smoothly and avoid rear‑end collisions.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When turning onto a street that has multiple lanes going your direction, which lane should you enter?
options: a:Turn into the lane closest to your previous lane.,b:Turn into the middle lane regardless of position.,c:Turn into the lane marked with an arrow (if present).
note: When turning onto a street with multiple lanes going your direction, you must turn into the lane that is closest to the lane you came from. This keeps traffic organized and prevents conflicts with vehicles turning from other directions or traveling in adjacent lanes.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What does a flashing yellow arrow for left turns allow you to do?
options: a:Merge into the lane in the direction of the arrow.,b:Come to a complete stop before turning.,c:Turn left after yielding to oncoming traffic and pedestrians.
note: A flashing yellow left-turn arrow means you may make the left turn, but it is not protected. You must yield to oncoming traffic, bicyclists, and pedestrians, and only turn when the way is clear.

question: If you suffer a tire blowout while driving, what is the correct immediate action?
options: a:Do not immediately apply your brakes.,b:Gradually slow down and pull off the side of the road.,c:Take your foot off the gas.
note: In a tire blowout, keep a firm grip on the steering wheel and do NOT slam on the brakes, because hard braking can cause loss of control. Instead, let off the gas so the vehicle slows gradually, then steer smoothly to the side of the road and stop in a safe place.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Where is passing never permitted?
options: a:When approaching an intersection.,b:On a hill or curve.,c:When school bus lights are flashing.
note: You must never pass a stopped school bus when its red lights are flashing and the stop arm is extended; traffic in most or all directions must stop because children may be crossing. Passing on hills or curves and near intersections is often illegal or unsafe, but the school bus with flashing red lights is an absolute no‑passing situation.

question: When stopped for a traffic violation or equipment check, you must produce which documents?
options: a:Proof of registration only,b:Proof of insurance only,c:Your license, proof of registration, and proof of insurance,d:No documents are required
note: When an officer stops you for a violation or equipment check, you are generally required to show your driver license, the vehicle’s registration, and proof of financial responsibility (insurance). Keeping these documents accessible helps the stop go smoothly and legally.

question: What practice best ensures safety when backing your vehicle?
options: a:Check your rearview mirrors only.,b:Check behind the vehicle on foot before you get into the driver's seat.,c:Honk your horn before shifting into reverse.
note: Before backing, walk behind your vehicle to check for children, pedestrians, or objects that may be hidden from view. After checking, back up slowly while looking over your shoulder and using mirrors; never rely on mirrors alone.

question: If you become stranded in a snowstorm, what is the best action?
options: a:Get out of the vehicle and walk for help,b:Stay in your car and wait for assistance,c:Lay down and sleep in the car,d:Walk into the road to attract attention
note: Staying in your vehicle during a snowstorm is usually safest. Your car offers shelter from cold and wind, makes you easier for rescuers to find, and reduces the risk of getting lost or hit by other vehicles in low visibility.

question: What should car drivers remember about large trucks?
options: a:They have large blind spots and need more room to maneuver and stop.,b:They can stop more quickly than passenger vehicles.,c:They do not need more room to maneuver than passenger cars.
