note: Large trucks have big blind spots on all sides, especially directly behind and along both sides near the cab. They also need more distance to stop and more space to turn and maneuver. Give them extra room and avoid lingering beside them.

question: If another driver behaves aggressively and cuts you off, what is the safest immediate response?
options: a:Flash your vehicle's lights to let the aggressive driver know they are wrong.,b:Stay calm and move out of the aggressive driver's way.,c:Call the police immediately.
note: When another driver is aggressive, your priority is to avoid conflict and stay safe. Stay calm, do not make eye contact or gestures, and safely move out of their way. Escalating the situation can lead to road rage and crashes.

question: How can you avoid the risks of alcohol-related crashes?
options: a:Use a taxi, rideshare, public transit, or a designated driver instead of driving after drinking.,b:Decide before you start drinking that you will not drive and arrange a sober ride.,c:Only accept one drink so you can still drive safely.
note: The safest way to avoid an alcohol‑related crash is to plan ahead: decide before you drink that you will not drive and arrange a sober way home. Once you start drinking, your judgment is impaired, so pre‑planning is critical. Taxis, rideshares, or designated drivers are good tools, but they only work if you have already decided you will not drive after drinking.

question: What should you do when you see a school crossing sign?
options: a:Always sound your horn.,b:Watch for children and be ready to stop.,c:Always stop regardless of conditions.
note: A school crossing sign warns that children may be crossing the road. You must slow down, watch carefully for children, obey crossing guards and signals, and be prepared to stop whenever children are present or crossing.

question: Which pavement or lane marking is commonly used to direct drivers into the proper lanes for turning?
options: a:Painted arrows in the lanes.,b:Flashing red lights.,c:White lines on the side of the road.
note: Painted arrows in the lanes are used to show which movements are allowed from each lane, such as left turn only, right turn only, or straight ahead. Drivers should be in the correct lane before reaching the intersection and follow the direction of the arrows.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What must a driver do when approaching a flashing red traffic signal?
options: a:Stop, yield to traffic and pedestrians, then go when it is safe.,b:Slow down and proceed without stopping.,c:Merge to the right and continue without stopping.
note: A flashing red light is treated the same as a stop sign. You must come to a complete stop, check for cross traffic and pedestrians, yield the right-of-way as required, and proceed only when the intersection is clear and it is safe.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which is true about crosswalks?
options: a:Crosswalks always have horizontal pavement markings,b:They may be marked or unmarked and still exist legally,c:Crosswalks are always unmarked,d:Vertical pavement markings indicate crosswalks
note: A crosswalk can be either marked with painted lines or unmarked at an intersection. Legally, pedestrians may have the right-of-way in both marked and unmarked crosswalks, and drivers must be prepared to stop for pedestrians crossing at these locations.

question: If a driver's left arm and hand are extended downward, what does that signal mean?
options: a:Intend to stop,b:Intend to turn left,c:Intend to turn right,d:Intend to back up
note: Hand signals are used when turn signals are not working or for added clarity. A left arm extended downward with the palm facing to the rear means the driver intends to slow or stop. When you see this, be prepared to reduce speed and allow extra space.

question: When there are two railroad tracks next to each other, what must you remember after one train passes?
options: a:It is always safe to proceed after one train passes.,b:Look for another train on the other track before proceeding.,c:You must always stop before crossing regardless of signals.
note: At crossings with more than one track, one train passing can hide another train coming from either direction on the other track. After the first train clears, look and listen carefully for a second train and only proceed when you are sure all tracks are clear.

question: To cross a railroad safely you should:
options: a:Look both ways only when a red light is flashing,b:Listen and look both ways and proceed only when safe,c:Cross quickly when a train is approaching,d:Trust that gates will always signal an approaching train
note: At railroad crossings you must always look and listen for trains in both directions and only cross when you are sure it is safe. Never rely solely on lights or gates, and never try to beat a train.

question: Anything that causes you to do which of the following could lead to a crash?
options: a:Take your hands off the wheel,b:Take your eyes off the road,c:Take your attention away from driving,d:Any of the above
note: Any distraction that takes your hands off the wheel, your eyes off the road, or your mind off driving increases your risk of a crash. Safe driving requires full control, constant observation, and focused attention.

question: If an oncoming vehicle fails to dim high beams, where should you direct your gaze?
options: a:Toward the center of the road.,b:Toward the right side of the road.,c:Either side of the road.
note: When an oncoming driver does not dim high beams, briefly glance toward the right side of your lane and use the edge line or right side of the road as a guide. This reduces glare while still letting you stay in your lane safely.

question: When driving in fog, which lights should you use?
options: a:High beams,b:Low beams,c:Parking lights,d:Hazard lights
note: In fog, use low beam headlights (and fog lights if your vehicle has them). High beams reflect off the fog and make it harder to see, while low beams light the road ahead without as much glare.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Approaching an uncontrolled intersection, how should you prepare to avoid a crash?
options: a:Maintain your speed and proceed.,b:Slow, cover the brake, and look left, right, and left again, yielding as necessary to avoid a collision.,c:Yield to all other drivers regardless of the situation.
note: At an uncontrolled intersection, slow down, be ready to brake, and look left, right, and left again. Yield as needed, especially to vehicles already in the intersection and to vehicles approaching from your right, so you can avoid a collision.

question: Which statement about drowsy drivers is correct?
options: a:Opening a window and turning up the radio is usually enough to stay alert,b:Drowsy drivers can appear impaired like drunk drivers,c:Drinking strong coffee reliably prevents drowsiness,d:Drowsiness improves reaction time
note: Drowsiness can slow your reactions, impair judgment, and cause lane drifting in ways very similar to alcohol impairment. Opening a window, turning up the radio, or drinking coffee are not reliable ways to stay alert; the only real solution to drowsiness is rest.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When driving on an interstate, which practice is correct before changing lanes?
options: a:Signal, check mirrors, and check blind spots,b:Always use cruise control,c:Stop on the shoulder if you feel tired,d:Change lanes frequently to maintain speed
note: Before changing lanes at any speed, especially on interstates, you must signal, check your mirrors, and then check your blind spot by looking over your shoulder. Cruise control should only be used when conditions are safe, and you should not stop on the shoulder unless it is an emergency.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What does double solid yellow centerline pavement marking indicate?
options: a:Passing is not permitted from either direction except for certain turning movements when safe.,b:Passing is allowed for drivers from both directions.,c:Passing is allowed only during daylight.
note: A double solid yellow centerline means vehicles in both directions are prohibited from crossing the lines to pass other vehicles. You may usually cross these lines only to turn left into or out of a driveway or side road when it is safe and legal to do so, but not to pass moving traffic.

question: What should you do when driving on slippery roads?
options: a:Increase your following distance.,b:Use alternate routes.,c:Drive as you would on dry roads.
note: On slippery roads, your tires have less traction, so it takes longer to stop and easier to skid. Increasing your following distance and reducing speed gives you more time and space to react and brake gently, helping you maintain control.

question: If other drivers around you are acting angrily, what should you do?
options: a:Don't make eye contact.,b:Don't react with hand gestures.,c:Distance yourself from the situation (all of the above).
note: When other drivers are angry or aggressive, avoid eye contact and do not respond with gestures or aggressive behavior. Instead, create space by safely slowing down, changing lanes, or exiting the roadway so you are no longer near the aggressive driver.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When entering the roadway from a private road or driveway, what must you do?
options: a:Blow your horn to warn approaching vehicles.,b:Drive out fast to merge smoothly with traffic.,c:Yield the right-of-way to pedestrians and traffic on the roadway.
note: When you enter a public road from a private road, driveway, or alley, you must yield to all pedestrians and vehicles already on the roadway. They have the right-of-way, and you may proceed only when it is safe and will not force others to slow or change lanes suddenly.

question: If a driver's left arm and hand are extended upward, what does this hand signal indicate?
options: a:Intends to turn right,b:Intends to turn left,c:Intends to stop,d:Intends to reverse
note: Standard hand signals are used when turn signals are not working or are hard to see. A left arm straight out means a left turn, a left arm bent upward at the elbow means a right turn, and a left arm bent downward means slowing or stopping. If you see a driver’s left arm and hand extended upward, you should expect them to turn right and adjust your speed and position accordingly.

question: If you turn onto a two-lane road divided by a broken yellow line, what do you know immediately?
options: a:You are on a two-way road.,b:You are on a one-way road.,c:The road is under repair.
note: A broken yellow centerline means traffic on the road is moving in opposite directions, so it is a two-way road. Yellow lines always separate opposing directions of travel; white lines separate traffic moving in the same direction. A broken yellow line also means passing is allowed when it is safe and not otherwise prohibited.

question: An 'End school zone' sign indicates what?
options: a:The beginning of a reduced speed school zone.,b:The end of a reduced speed school zone.,c:The speed limit is now 20 mph.
note: An “End school zone” sign tells you that the special reduced speed limit for the school zone is over. After passing this sign, you may resume the regular posted speed limit for that area, but only if there is no other sign indicating a different speed.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When parallel parking, how close should your wheels be to the curb?
options: a:Within 10 inches.,b:Within 12 inches.,c:Within 18 inches.
note: When parallel parked, your wheels should be parallel to and within 12 inches of the curb.

question: If it starts to sleet or snow while you're driving, you should:
options: a:Keep your windshield and mirrors clear,b:Increase speed to reach your destination sooner,c:Follow closely to the vehicle ahead to improve traction,d:Turn off your headlights
note: In sleet or snow, keep your windshield, windows, and mirrors clear so you can see, turn on your low‑beam headlights, slow down, and increase your following distance. Stopping distances are much longer on slippery roads, so give yourself more space and time to react.

question: If you begin to lose traction on a slippery road and need to slow down, what should you do first?
options: a:Firmly apply your brakes.,b:Take your foot off the gas (ease off the accelerator).,c:Apply your parking brake immediately.
note: On a slippery surface, the first and safest action when you start to lose traction is to ease off the accelerator. This lets the tires regain grip. If you still need to slow more, brake gently and progressively to avoid skidding; sudden or hard braking can cause loss of control.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If turning left onto a one-way street, into which lane should you complete the turn?
options: a:The lane closest to your previous lane,b:The right lane,c:Either lane as long as it's clear,d:The far left lane only
note: When turning left onto a one‑way street, you must turn into the lane closest to the one you turned from, as long as it is a legal lane for travel. This keeps traffic organized and predictable and reduces the chance of sideswipe or angle collisions.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When two vehicles arrive at an intersection from different highways at the same time, which vehicle must yield?
options: a:Either one may go first.,b:The vehicle on the left must yield to the vehicle on the right.,c:The vehicle on the right must yield to the vehicle on the left.
note: At an uncontrolled intersection where two vehicles arrive at the same time, the driver on the left must yield to the driver on the right. This right‑of‑way rule helps decide who goes first and prevents confusion and collisions.

question: Which technique helps avoid crashes on icy or snowy roads?
options: a:Engage four-wheel drive and reduce speed as needed,b:Get off highways as quickly as possible,c:Add extra weight to the vehicle for traction,d:Drive at normal speeds but use lower gears
note: On icy or snowy roads, the key safety technique is to slow down and increase following distance. If your vehicle has four‑wheel drive, using it can improve traction for starting and climbing, but it does not shorten stopping distance. Even with four‑wheel drive, you must drive more slowly and smoothly than on dry roads.

question: Which statement about seat belts and child restraints is correct?
options: a:Never place a rear-facing infant restraint in the front seat of a vehicle with a passenger airbag.,b:You should never place any child in a rear seat.,c:Airbags make it safe to place infants in front seats.
note: Children are safest in the back seat, especially those 12 and under, and all children must be properly restrained in an appropriate child safety seat or seat belt. A rear‑facing infant seat must never be placed in front of an active passenger airbag because the airbag can strike the back of the seat and seriously injure or kill the infant.

question: When parking downhill on a two-way street, how should you position your front wheels?
options: a:Turn your wheels to the right (toward the curb).,b:Keep your wheels pointed straight ahead.,c:Turn your wheels to the left (away from the curb).
note: When parking downhill on a two‑way street with a curb, turn the front wheels toward the curb and set the parking brake. If the vehicle rolls, the front tire will hit the curb and stop the car from rolling into traffic.

question: Approximately how far might a fully loaded tractor-trailer traveling at 55 mph take to come to a complete stop?
options: a:50 feet,b:125 feet,c:400 feet
note: Large trucks need much more distance to stop than passenger cars. A fully loaded tractor‑trailer traveling about 55 mph may need roughly the length of a football field or more—around 400 feet—to come to a complete stop under good conditions.

question: How does smoking or preparing to smoke while driving affect your driving?
options: a:Helps maintain driver alertness.,b:Does not affect driving abilities.,c:Is a distracting activity.
note: Smoking or preparing to smoke while driving is a distraction because it takes at least one hand off the wheel and can draw your eyes and attention away from the road. Any activity that diverts your hands, eyes, or mind from driving increases crash risk.

question: What does the term “No zone” refer to?
options: a:A roadway with restrictions on vehicle stereo volume.,b:A term used to describe blind spots around a truck or bus.,c:A special speed zone.
note: The “No‑Zone” is the large blind‑spot area around trucks and buses where the driver cannot see you in their mirrors. Staying out of these areas—especially directly behind, alongside the trailer, and close in front—helps the truck or bus driver see you and reduces the chance of a collision.

question: When driving on major highways, what should you do to stay safe?
options: a:Stay alert,b:Keep your eyes moving,c:Be ready to react to hazards,d:All of the above
note: On highways you must stay mentally alert, keep your eyes moving to scan far ahead and to the sides, and be ready to react quickly to any hazard. Doing all of these together helps prevent highway hypnosis and gives you more time to avoid crashes.

question: How can you help ensure your physical condition does not make you an unsafe driver?
options: a:Know the effects of any medicine on your driving ability.,b:Keep physically fit and have regular medical checkups.,c:Do all of the above.
note: Your physical and medical condition directly affects how safely you can drive. You should know how any medicines you take can affect alertness, vision, or coordination, and you should stay in good physical health with regular medical checkups. Doing all of these helps you recognize and manage any limitations before they become a safety risk.

question: Distracted drivers have a greater crash risk when using which device?
options: a:CD player,b:Radio,c:Cell phone,d:Air conditioning controls
note: Any in‑car device can distract you, but cell phone use is especially dangerous because it takes your attention and often your eyes and hands away from driving. Even hands‑free calls create mental distraction and significantly increase crash risk, so you should avoid using a phone while driving whenever possible.

question: Why is driving at night often more difficult than daytime driving?
options: a:It is more likely to be raining at night.,b:Visibility is reduced in the dark.,c:Cars overheat more quickly at night.
note: Night driving is harder mainly because you cannot see as far or as clearly. Headlights limit your field of vision, and glare from other vehicles can further reduce visibility. Use proper headlights, reduce your speed, and always drive so you can stop within the distance you can see ahead.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When passing another vehicle on a multilane highway, what must you be sure of first?
options: a:That the passing lane is clear and it is safe to move over.,b:That you pass only on the right.,c:That oncoming traffic is slowing down.
note: Before passing on a multilane highway, you must first make sure the lane you will move into is clear and that it is safe to change lanes. Check mirrors and blind spots, signal, and only move over when you have enough space to pass safely without exceeding the speed limit.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which statement about emergency vehicles is correct when they are using sirens and flashing lights?
options: a:May use a loudspeaker to give instructions.,b:Have the right-of-way when using sirens, horns, and/or flashing lights.,c:May follow each other.
note: Emergency vehicles using a siren and/or flashing lights have the right‑of‑way. You must yield by moving out of their path, following any instructions they give, and remembering that more than one emergency vehicle may be coming.

question: What should you do to safely pass a bicyclist?
options: a:Drive in the bicycle lane until you can pass.,b:Honk at the bicyclist to alert them.,c:Slow down and give as much space as possible when passing.
note: When passing a bicyclist, slow down and give them as much space as possible, following your state’s minimum passing distance (often at least 3 feet, and more at higher speeds). Never drive in the bike lane to pass, and avoid honking in a way that could startle the rider.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When you hear a siren or see flashing lights from an approaching emergency vehicle, what must you do?
options: a:Drive to the right side of the road and stop.,b:Slow down until it passes you.,c:Motion for the emergency vehicle to pass you.
note: When an emergency vehicle approaches using a siren and/or flashing lights, you must pull over to the right side of the road and stop, unless you are in an intersection. If you are in an intersection, clear it first, then pull over and remain stopped until the vehicle has passed.

question: Which of the following can impair your ability to drive?
options: a:Alcohol,b:Any medication,c:Lack of sleep,d:All of the above
note: Alcohol, many medications (including some over‑the‑counter and prescription drugs), and lack of sleep can all slow your reactions, affect judgment, and reduce awareness. Because any of these can make driving unsafe, you must be cautious and avoid driving when impaired.

question: On a highway marked by two solid yellow centerlines, when is it permissible to cross them?
options: a:To pass other vehicles when there is no oncoming traffic.,b:To cross only to make a left turn into or from an alley, private road, or driveway.,c:Under no circumstances.
note: Two solid yellow centerlines mean no passing in either direction. You may only cross them to make a left turn into or from a driveway, alley, or private road, or when specifically directed by traffic control or law enforcement.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If a green arrow at an intersection changes to a steady green light, what must you do before turning in that direction?
options: a:You may still turn but must yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians.,b:You may no longer turn and must proceed straight.,c:You still have the arrow's right-of-way without yielding.
note: When a green arrow turns into a steady green light, you may still turn in the direction of the arrow, but you no longer have a protected turn. You must yield to oncoming traffic, bicyclists, and pedestrians in the crosswalk, and only turn when it is safe.

question: When must drivers yield to pedestrians?
options: a:Even if the pedestrian crosses carelessly.,b:Only when the pedestrian is in a crosswalk.,c:Only if the pedestrian is on the same side of the road as the driver.
note: Drivers must always prioritize pedestrian safety. Even if a pedestrian is crossing carelessly or against a signal, you must slow down, be prepared to stop, and yield as needed to avoid hitting them. You are still responsible for preventing a collision.

question: If you are in traffic crossing a railroad track with no signals or gates, what must you ensure?
options: a:You have space to get completely across the tracks without stopping.,b:You may pass slower drivers while crossing.,c:You have the right-of-way and do not need to check for trains.
note: Never enter a railroad crossing unless you are sure you can completely clear the tracks without stopping. In traffic, wait until there is enough space on the far side so your entire vehicle can get across safely and you will not be forced to stop on the tracks.

question: If you're in an accident and your vehicle blocks traffic, you should:
options: a:Move your vehicle off the traveled portion of the roadway if possible,b:Wait until police arrive before moving anything,c:Never move the vehicle under any circumstances,d:Drive away if the damage is minor
note: If you are in a crash and your vehicle is blocking traffic but can be moved, you should move it off the traveled portion of the road to reduce the risk of another collision. Stay at the scene, exchange information, and provide help as required by law.

question: Why must you use extra caution when driving near a pedestrian using a white cane or guide dog?
options: a:They are likely deaf.,b:They might be directing traffic.,c:They are blind or visually impaired and need right-of-way.
note: A person using a white cane or a guide dog is blind or visually impaired. You must use extra caution, slow down, and yield the right-of-way, stopping if necessary, because they may not be able to see you or react quickly to unsafe situations.

question: Orange-colored signs are used to indicate what?
options: a:Work zones,b:Regulatory requirements,c:School zones,d:Scenic routes
note: Orange signs are temporary warning signs used for road work and construction zones. They alert drivers to workers, lane shifts, reduced speeds, and other changes in normal traffic patterns so drivers can slow down and proceed carefully.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which signal tells you to slow down and proceed with caution at an intersection?
options: a:A flashing yellow light.,b:A flashing red light.,c:A solid yellow light.
note: A flashing yellow light means you must slow down and proceed through the intersection with caution, watching carefully for other vehicles and pedestrians. You do not have to stop, but you must be prepared to stop if needed.

question: Why is maintaining a space cushion around your vehicle important?
options: a:Prevents distractions from other vehicles.,b:Allows you time to react to unexpected situations.,c:Keeps traffic flowing at a safe pace.
note: Maintaining a space cushion means leaving enough room around your vehicle so you have time and space to react. If another driver brakes suddenly, swerves, or makes a mistake, that extra distance helps you slow, stop, or steer away safely.

question: Driving while distracted by any activity usually causes which effect?
options: a:It is never dangerous,b:Drivers react more slowly to hazards,c:Drivers tend to speed up,d:It improves focus on the road
note: Distractions such as phone use, eating, or adjusting controls take your eyes, mind, or hands away from driving. This slows your reaction time and reduces your awareness of hazards, making crashes more likely.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Under which condition can you legally pass another vehicle on the right?
options: a:If there is an available passing lane and the other vehicle is turning left or waiting to turn left.,b:Even if it requires driving off the pavement.,c:On a narrow bridge.
note: You may pass on the right only when there is a clearly marked lane or enough paved space and the other vehicle is turning left or waiting to turn left. You must stay on the roadway and never drive off the pavement or onto the shoulder to pass.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which must you obey over the others: a steady red light, a police officer, or a stop sign?
options: a:A steady red light,b:A police officer,c:A stop sign
note: Directions from a police officer or other authorized person directing traffic always override traffic lights and signs. If an officer tells you to proceed through a red light or ignore a stop sign, you must follow the officer’s instructions because they are managing traffic for safety in that moment.

question: When parallel parking between two cars, what should you do first?
options: a:Pull up even with the car in front of the space,b:Turn your wheels to the left immediately,c:Turn your wheels to the right immediately,d:Back in without aligning with the car ahead
note: To begin a proper parallel park, you first pull up alongside and roughly even with the vehicle in front of the space, leaving a safe gap (about 2–3 feet). From this aligned position you can then back slowly while turning the wheel, which gives you enough room to angle the car into the space without hitting the curb or the other vehicles.

question: Why should drivers be extra alert to motorcyclists, bicyclists, and pedestrians?
options: a:They can be difficult to see and may be less predictable,b:They obey different traffic laws,c:They always have the right-of-way,d:They travel at higher speeds than cars
note: Motorcycles, bicycles, and pedestrians are smaller and can be hidden in blind spots or by other vehicles, and they may move or change position more quickly or unexpectedly. Because they are also more vulnerable in a crash, drivers must scan carefully, check mirrors and blind spots, and anticipate that these road users may be harder to see and less predictable than cars.

question: What is the safest method to pass a bicyclist on a two-lane road with no bicycle lane?
options: a:Do not pass until you reach a traffic signal or stop sign.,b:Slow down and wait until there is no oncoming traffic, then pass leaving sufficient space.,c:Continue driving straight; it is the bicyclist’s responsibility to get out of your way.
note: On a two-lane road, you should treat a bicycle like any other vehicle when passing: slow down, wait until there is no oncoming traffic, then move over and pass only when it is safe. Leave at least 3 feet of space (or more at higher speeds or if required by state law) between your vehicle and the bicyclist, and return to your lane only after you have fully cleared the rider.

question: What usually causes hydroplaning?
options: a:Driving too fast on a wet surface,b:Excessive stops,c:Using cruise control,d:Low tire pressure only
note: Hydroplaning happens when you drive too fast on a wet surface and your tires cannot push the water away quickly enough. A thin layer of water builds up under the tires, lifting them off the road so you lose steering and braking control. Slowing down in rain, especially in standing water, is the best way to prevent hydroplaning.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If two vehicles arrive at a four-way stop at the same time, who has the right-of-way?
options: a:The vehicle on the left must go first,b:The vehicle on the right has the right-of-way,c:The bigger vehicle has right-of-way,d:Drivers should signal each other to decide
note: At a four-way stop, if two vehicles arrive at the same time, the driver on the left must yield to the driver on the right. This means the vehicle on the right has the right-of-way and should proceed first.

question: When should you increase your following distance?
options: a:When conditions reduce your ability to see or stop in time (e.g., behind large vehicles, in bad weather, at higher speeds, or in heavy traffic).,b:Only when exiting an expressway.,c:Only when following another car closely in clear weather.
note: You should increase your following distance whenever conditions make it harder to see or stop in time. This includes driving behind large vehicles that block your view, in bad weather, at higher speeds, in heavy traffic, or when following motorcycles or vehicles that may stop suddenly.

question: How can you reduce the risk of hydroplaning on wet roads?
options: a:Slow down on wet roads and avoid driving through standing water.,b:Drive through shallow water at normal or reduced speed.,c:Speed up to get through water more quickly.
note: Hydroplaning happens when your tires ride on a thin layer of water and lose contact with the road, usually at higher speeds. To reduce the risk, slow down on wet roads, especially in heavy rain or standing water, and make sure your tires are properly inflated and have good tread.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When an emergency vehicle using sirens and/or flashing lights approaches, you must immediately:
options: a:Pull to the right and stop,b:Pull to the right and slow down only,c:Turn on your vehicle's four-way flashers and maintain speed,d:Pull to the left and stop
note: When an emergency vehicle with flashing lights and/or siren approaches from any direction, you must yield the right-of-way by pulling as close as safely possible to the right edge of the road and stopping until it has passed, unless directed otherwise by a police officer.

question: Which quality describes a good defensive driver?
options: a:Always driving slowly regardless of conditions,b:Looking out for actions of other drivers,c:Keeping a constant speed at all times,d:Never using mirrors
note: A good defensive driver constantly scans the road and watches the actions of other drivers, pedestrians, and cyclists. By anticipating what others might do, you have more time to react and can avoid collisions, rather than assuming everyone will always follow the rules.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What does a posted speed limit represent?
options: a:The maximum or minimum legal speed you can travel on a road under dangerous conditions.,b:The suggested speed to travel on a road under ideal conditions.,c:The maximum legal speed under ideal conditions.
note: A posted speed limit is the maximum legal speed allowed on that road in ideal conditions. You must slow down below the limit when weather, traffic, or road conditions make the posted speed unsafe.

question: If your vehicle is not equipped with ABS and you must stop quickly, what should you do?
options: a:Hold down the brake pedal.,b:Firmly pump the brakes.,c:Lightly tap the brakes.
note: In a vehicle without ABS, you should firmly pump the brakes to slow quickly without locking the wheels. Pumping lets the tires keep rolling so you can still steer while braking hard.

question: Which behavior describes an inattentive driver?
options: a:Staring off the roadway or daydreaming while driving,b:Maintaining eye contact with a passenger during a conversation,c:Only watching the vehicle directly ahead,d:Using cruise control appropriately
note: An inattentive driver is mentally or visually distracted from the driving task, such as staring off the roadway or daydreaming instead of actively scanning traffic and road conditions.

question: Before changing lanes, what checks should you make?
options: a:Check your side and rearview mirrors.,b:Give a turn signal to indicate your intentions.,c:All of the above
note: Before changing lanes, you should check your mirrors, signal your intention, and check your blind spots for other vehicles that may be entering the same lane. Using all three steps helps prevent conflicts with vehicles you cannot see in your mirrors alone.

question: Regulatory signs generally do what?
options: a:Warn of present danger,b:Indicate what a driver must or must not do,c:Are diamond-shaped and yellow,d:Are only used on highways
note: Regulatory signs tell you what you must do or must not do, such as speed limits, stop, yield, or no-turn signs. They are used to enforce traffic laws and rules of the road.

question: What should you do when visibility is reduced by fog?
options: a:Turn on your low beam headlights.,b:Turn on your hazard lights and continue at the speed limit.,c:Use high beams for better visibility.
note: Use low-beam headlights in fog because their light is aimed lower and causes less glare off the water droplets. High beams reflect off the fog and can make it harder to see. Drive at a safe speed for the conditions and be prepared to slow or stop if visibility becomes very poor.

question: If a fire engine is following you but is not using emergency lights or siren, how should you respond?
options: a:Stop as quickly as you can.,b:Continue to drive in a normal manner.,c:Speed up to get out of its way.
note: You are only required to yield and pull over for emergency vehicles when they are using their lights and/or siren. If a fire engine is behind you without lights or siren, treat it like any other vehicle: follow all normal traffic laws, maintain a safe speed and following distance, and do not brake suddenly or speed up unnecessarily.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When you see a steady yellow arrow pointing for a turn, what should you do?
options: a:May complete the turn if you are too close to stop safely, after yielding to oncoming traffic and pedestrians.,b:Should slow down and prepare to stop if it is safe to do so.,c:Must immediately merge into the lane indicated by the arrow.
note: A steady yellow arrow means the protected turn movement is ending and a red arrow is about to appear. You should slow down and prepare to stop if you can do so safely. If you are already too close to the intersection to stop safely, you may complete the turn with caution before the signal changes to red.

question: What are highway signs called that require drivers to obey the indicated instruction?
options: a:Warning signs.,b:Regulatory signs.,c:Information signs.
note: Regulatory signs tell you what you must do or must not do under the law, such as speed limits, stop signs, yield signs, and no-turn signs. Ignoring regulatory signs can result in traffic tickets or other penalties.

question: What is a \No zone\" with regard to large vehicles?"
options: a:A designated no-passing zone marked on the roadway.,b:A restricted lane reserved only for trucks and buses.,c:The large blind-spot areas around a truck or bus where the driver cannot see you.
note: A "No-Zone" is the large blind-spot area around trucks and other large vehicles where the driver cannot see you in their mirrors. These areas are along the sides, directly behind, and sometimes directly in front of the vehicle. Avoid driving in these zones whenever possible, and pass through them quickly and safely so the truck driver can see you.

question: A person using a white cane or a guide dog is most likely to be which of the following?
options: a:Part of a traffic study,b:A deaf person,c:A blind person,d:A pedestrian crossing guard
note: A white cane or a guide dog is the standard indicator that a pedestrian is blind or visually impaired. Drivers must always yield the right‑of‑way, stop well in advance, and use extra caution around these pedestrians.

question: What is the best way to handle a driver tailgating you?
options: a:Slam on your brakes to make them back off.,b:Change lanes or gradually reduce speed to encourage them to pass.,c:Speed up to increase distance from the tailgater.
note: When someone is tailgating, the safest response is to make it easy for them to pass: change lanes when safe or gradually reduce speed to encourage them to go around you. Never brake suddenly or speed up, as both can increase the risk of a crash.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If an intersection is blocked by traffic ahead, what should you do?
options: a:Enter slowly until the traffic clears.,b:Get as close as possible to the car in front of you.,c:Stay out of the intersection until you can pass completely through.
note: You must not enter an intersection unless you can drive all the way through without stopping. Entering when traffic is blocked can leave you stuck in the intersection, which is illegal in many areas and can block cross traffic.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What does a solid red arrow on a traffic signal mean?
options: a:It is never used as a traffic signal.,b:It has the same meaning as a circular red light; you must stop and may not turn in the arrow's direction.,c:It means drivers may turn in the arrow's direction.
note: A solid red arrow means you must stop and remain stopped. You may not turn in the direction of the arrow until it changes to green or a permissive signal. It functions like a red light specifically for that turning movement.

question: As alcohol accumulates in your blood, it typically does what?
options: a:Slows reactions and increases confidence,b:Speeds up your metabolism,c:Improves your coordination,d:Reduces the effect of other drugs
note: As blood alcohol concentration rises, reaction time slows, coordination and judgment worsen, and many people feel more confident than they should. This false confidence combined with slower reactions makes driving extremely dangerous.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: A flashing red traffic signal means you must:
options: a:Come to a complete stop, yield as required, then go when safe (same as a stop sign).,b:Drive through cautiously without stopping.,c:Treat it as a flashing yellow light.
note: A flashing red light means the same as a stop sign: you must come to a complete stop, yield to any traffic or pedestrians with the right‑of‑way, and then proceed only when it is safe.

question: If you're angry after an incident at work, what should you do before driving?
options: a:Drive fast to let off steam,b:Play loud music to distract yourself,c:Take a few minutes to calm down before you drive,d:Call someone and continue driving while talking
note: Strong emotions like anger can lead to aggressive or careless driving. Before driving, take a few minutes to calm down so you can focus on the road and make safe decisions.

question: To avoid a large truck or bus blind spot, what should you do?
options: a:Flash your lights at them.,b:Avoid driving alongside them and avoid tailgating.,c:Never pass them.,d:Pass safely and promptly; don’t linger in their blind spots.
note: Large trucks and buses have big blind spots along both sides and directly behind them. Stay out of these areas by not lingering alongside the vehicle and never tailgating; if you can’t see the driver’s mirrors, they likely can’t see you.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If traffic signals at an intersection are not functioning due to a power outage, how should drivers behave?
options: a:Treat the intersection as a four-way stop and yield in turn.,b:Turn on hazard lights and proceed without stopping.,c:Park and wait for power to be restored.
note: When traffic signals are completely out, treat the intersection as a four‑way stop. Come to a full stop, then proceed in the order of arrival; if you arrive at the same time as another driver, yield to the vehicle on your right.

question: When changing lanes on a highway, which sequence is correct?
options: a:Check mirrors, signal, then check blind spot,b:Signal, check rearview and outside mirrors, and glance over your shoulder to check blind spots,c:Quickly turn your head without signaling,d:Change lanes without signaling if traffic is light
note: Before changing lanes, always signal first to alert others, then check your mirrors and quickly glance over your shoulder to check your blind spot. Only move into the lane when it is clear and safe.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: While waiting in an intersection to complete a left turn, how should you position your front wheels?
options: a:Signal and keep your wheels turned to the left.,b:Signal and keep your wheels straight.,c:Flash your headlights to tell drivers to let you through.
note: Keep your front wheels straight while waiting to turn left. If your wheels are turned left and you are hit from behind, your vehicle can be pushed into oncoming traffic. With wheels straight, a rear-end impact is less likely to send you into opposing lanes.

question: Which is a likely consequence of driving with worn or bald tires?
options: a:They can increase your stopping distance.,b:They improve traction on wet roads.,c:They reduce the chance of hydroplaning.
note: Tires with worn or bald tread cannot grip the road well. This increases your stopping distance, makes it harder to steer and control the vehicle, and greatly raises the risk of skidding or hydroplaning on wet roads.

question: A yellow and black diamond-shaped sign is used to:
options: a:Warn you about conditions on or near the road ahead.,b:Provide directions to towns and cities.,c:State traffic laws and regulations.
note: Yellow and black diamond-shaped signs are warning signs. They alert you to hazards or changes in road conditions ahead, such as curves, intersections, or pedestrian crossings, so you can slow down and proceed with caution.

question: Alcoholic beverages can affect you by doing which of the following?
options: a:Slowing your reaction time,b:Giving you false confidence,c:Impeding your thinking ability,d:All of the above
note: Alcohol affects many parts of your driving ability at once. It slows your reaction time, makes you overconfident, and interferes with clear thinking and judgment. Because all of these effects occur together, any amount of drinking can make driving unsafe.

question: What is the effect of taking drugs along with alcohol?
options: a:It increases the risk of causing a crash,b:It is no more dangerous than alcohol alone,c:It lessens alcohol's effect on driving,d:It negates impairment
note: Using alcohol with any other drug—prescription, over-the-counter, or illegal—can greatly increase impairment. The substances can interact in unpredictable ways, making you much less able to judge, react, and control your vehicle, and sharply increasing crash risk.

question: Which shape of sign warns of an upcoming railroad crossing?
options: a:A round sign.,b:A school zone sign.,c:A no-passing sign.
note: Round (circular) warning signs are used to alert drivers that a railroad crossing is ahead. When you see a round railroad warning sign, slow down, look and listen for trains, and be prepared to stop if necessary.

question: When parking uphill next to a curb, you should set the parking brake and:
options: a:Turn your steering wheel away from the curb.,b:Keep the front tires straight ahead.,c:Keep the rear tires against the curb.
note: When parking uphill with a curb, turn the front wheels away from the curb and set the parking brake. If the vehicle rolls, the back of the front tire will gently contact the curb and help stop the car from rolling into traffic.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you pass your exit while on the interstate, what should you do?
options: a:Quickly cut across traffic to reach the exit.,b:Make an immediate U-turn.,c:Continue to the next exit and safely return.
note: If you miss your exit on an interstate, stay calm, continue to the next exit, and then safely return using the proper ramps. Never stop on the roadway, back up, cut across traffic, or make a U-turn on the interstate.

question: If a tire blows out while you are driving, what is the correct response?
options: a:Brake hard immediately.,b:Try to steer straight while gradually slowing and ease off the gas.,c:Maintain your current speed and steer straight.
note: If a tire blows out, hold the steering wheel firmly, keep the vehicle going straight, and gradually ease off the accelerator. Do not brake hard; once the vehicle has slowed and you have control, brake gently and move off the road to a safe place.

question: If the solid white edge line on the right side of the roadway slants to the left, what does it indicate?
options: a:The road is about to become narrower ahead.,b:An intersection is just ahead.,c:You will be required to turn left soon.
note: A solid white edge line that angles toward the center of the road indicates that the usable roadway is narrowing ahead. This warns you to be prepared for less space and to adjust your speed and position accordingly.

question: Which statement about work zones is correct?
options: a:Work zones may be stationary or moving,b:Work zones are marked with black and white signs,c:Drivers are not required to slow down in work zones,d:Work zones are always closed to traffic
note: Work zones can be either stationary (like a fixed construction site) or moving (such as a line-painting or street-sweeping operation). They are usually marked with orange warning signs, cones, and other devices. Drivers must slow down, obey posted work zone speed limits, and be especially alert for workers and equipment.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If a steady yellow light appears while you are already in the intersection, what should you do?
options: a:Stop if you can do so safely before entering the intersection.,b:Speed up to get through the intersection before the light turns red.,c:Continue through the intersection carefully.
note: A steady yellow light warns that the signal is about to turn red. If the light turns yellow after you have already entered the intersection, you should continue through and clear the intersection safely. Do not stop suddenly in the intersection, because that can confuse or endanger drivers behind you.

question: If your wheels drop off the pavement onto the shoulder, what is the safest action?
options: a:Slow down and very carefully turn back onto the pavement.,b:Brake hard and turn sharply back onto the pavement.,c:Stop your car on the edge of the road.
note: If your wheels drop off the pavement onto the shoulder, stay calm and keep a firm grip on the wheel. Ease off the accelerator and slow down gradually; do not brake hard or jerk the steering wheel. When your speed is under control and traffic allows, gently steer back onto the pavement.

question: Which of the following does NOT affect vehicle stopping distance?
options: a:Your reaction time.,b:The time of day.,c:The condition of your vehicle's brakes.
note: Stopping distance is made up of your reaction distance and your braking distance. It is affected by how quickly you react, your speed, the condition of your brakes and tires, and road and weather conditions. The time of day by itself does not change how far your vehicle needs to stop.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: You may not park within how many feet of a crosswalk or intersection?
options: a:10 feet,b:25 feet,c:50 feet,d:15 feet
note: Many states prohibit parking within about 20–25 feet of a crosswalk or intersection so that drivers and pedestrians can see each other clearly. Always check your state’s specific distance, but you should leave a substantial clear space before a crosswalk or intersection and never park right up to the corner.

question: When may you cross a dashed white line painted on the road?
options: a:Only during daylight hours.,b:When it is safe to change lanes.,c:At any time even if unsafe.
note: Broken (dashed) white lines separate lanes of traffic moving in the same direction. You may cross them when you are changing lanes or merging, but only after checking mirrors and blind spots and making sure it is safe to move.

question: An orange-colored traffic sign is used to indicate what?
options: a:The start of a no passing zone.,b:Construction, maintenance, or emergency work ahead.,c:A school zone is ahead.
note: Orange traffic signs are used for temporary traffic control zones, such as construction, maintenance, or emergency work areas. They warn you to slow down, be alert, and be prepared for workers, equipment, or changed road conditions.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If the traffic light turns from green to solid yellow as you approach an intersection, what should you do?
options: a:Stop before entering the intersection if you can do so safely.,b:Consider it the same as a caution sign and always continue.,c:Stop immediately at any cost.
note: A solid yellow light means the signal is about to turn red. You must stop before entering the intersection if you can do so safely. If you are too close to stop safely when it turns yellow, continue through the intersection with caution instead of braking hard in the middle.

question: If the driver behind you wants to pass, how should you respond?
options: a:Speed up to prevent them from passing.,b:Go the same speed and maintain position.,c:Slow down to provide room in front for them to pass safely.
note: When another driver wants to pass you, help them do it safely. Maintain a steady speed or slow down slightly to create more space in front of you so they can return to the lane safely after passing. Never speed up to block a passing vehicle.

question: If an aggressive driver is following you closely, what should you do?
options: a:Stare at the driver as they pass.,b:Speed up as they pass to discourage them.,c:Try to get out of their way (slow down or change lanes).
note: If an aggressive driver is tailgating you, focus on safety and avoid confrontation. Move to another lane or gradually slow down to encourage them to pass. Do not make eye contact, gesture, or speed up, as this can escalate the situation.

question: A driver who travels much slower than the speed limit:
options: a:Always has the right-of-way,b:Is necessarily a very safe driver,c:Should allow following cars to pass if traffic is backing up,d:May ignore pullouts and continue slowly
note: Driving much slower than the normal flow of traffic can be dangerous because it can cause sudden braking, tailgating, and risky passing. On two-lane roads, if several vehicles are stacked up behind you, you should use a turnout or safely pull off the road to let them pass. This helps keep traffic flowing smoothly and reduces the risk of collisions.

question: If your vehicle begins to skid, what should you do?
options: a:Turn the steering wheel in the direction you want the front of the vehicle to go,b:Overcorrect rapidly,c:Turn your wheel opposite the skid,d:Brake hard immediately
note: When your vehicle begins to skid, stay calm, ease off the accelerator, and steer in the direction you want the front of the vehicle to go. This is often described as steering in the direction of the skid. Avoid slamming on the brakes or jerking the wheel, because sudden movements can make the skid worse and cause you to lose more control.

question: To reduce the effects of oncoming headlight glare at night, where should you look?
options: a:Straight ahead.,b:At the center of the road.,c:Toward the right side of the road ahead.
note: At night, bright oncoming headlights can temporarily blind you. To reduce glare, briefly look toward the right edge of your lane and use the right side of the road or the white edge line as a guide. Do not stare directly into the oncoming headlights, and do not close your eyes; keeping your focus slightly to the right helps you maintain a safe path while protecting your night vision.

question: When approaching railroad tracks, what should you do?
options: a:Look, listen, slow down, and be prepared to stop,b:Speed up to cross before a gate lowers,c:Try to drive around a lowered gate,d:Stop only if you see a train
note: Railroad crossings require extra caution because trains cannot stop quickly. As you approach tracks, slow down, look both ways, and listen for trains. Be prepared to stop if a train is approaching or warning devices are active. Never speed up to beat a train or drive around lowered gates; it is illegal and extremely dangerous.

question: A steady yellow traffic signal means that which light will soon appear?
options: a:A flashing yellow light,b:A steady red light,c:A steady green light,d:A flashing red light
note: A steady yellow traffic signal means the light is about to turn red. It warns you to slow down and stop if you can do so safely before entering the intersection. If you are too close to stop safely when the light turns yellow, proceed with caution through the intersection before the light turns red.

question: Is it ever acceptable to drive around or under a railroad crossing gate that is moving?
options: a:If your vehicle can do so without damaging the gate.,b:Only if an approaching train is not too close.,c:No — never drive around or under a lowering or raised gate.
note: You must never drive around, under, or through any railroad crossing gate, whether it is lowering, down, or starting to rise. Trains are large, fast, and cannot stop quickly, and signals can activate again if another train is coming. Always wait until the gates are fully raised and all warning lights and bells have stopped before proceeding.

question: Which of these does NOT promote safe night driving?
options: a:Keep your windshield clean.,b:Be aware that tinted windows reduce visibility at night.,c:Rely only on a flashlight carried in the vehicle.
note: Safe night driving depends on maximizing your ability to see and be seen. Keeping the windshield clean and avoiding dark or illegal window tint improves visibility. A flashlight can be useful in an emergency when stopped, but it is not a driving aid and you must never rely on it to see the road while driving; you must rely on your vehicle’s headlights and proper vision through the windows.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Unless posted otherwise, what is the maximum speed on a rural interstate highway?
options: a:40 mph,b:55 mph,c:Varies by state; obey the posted limit.,d:65 mph
note: Speed limits on rural interstate highways are set by each state and commonly range from 65 to 75 mph, with some states higher or lower. There is no single nationwide default of 75 mph. You must always follow the posted speed limit signs for the specific road and area you are driving in, and adjust your speed for traffic, weather, and road conditions even if that means driving below the posted maximum.

question: At night, which road user is the hardest to see?
options: a:Other motorists.,b:Pedestrians.,c:Road signs.
note: At night, pedestrians are often the hardest road users to see because they are smaller than vehicles and may wear dark clothing or be outside the beam of your headlights. Road signs are usually reflective, and other vehicles have lights, making them easier to detect. Always scan carefully for pedestrians at night, especially near crosswalks, intersections, and along the roadway.

question: What danger can a leaking exhaust system create for vehicle occupants?
options: a:Cause excessive oil use.,b:Require your vehicle to have a tune-up sooner.,c:Make you drowsy and expose you to toxic fumes.
note: A leaking exhaust system can allow carbon monoxide and other harmful gases to enter the passenger compartment. Carbon monoxide is colorless and odorless and can cause headache, dizziness, drowsiness, unconsciousness, and even death. If you suspect an exhaust leak, have the vehicle inspected and repaired immediately and avoid driving it with windows closed.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: You must stop at an intersection when you see which of the following signals?
options: a:A flashing red light.,b:A steady yellow light.,c:A yellow arrow.
note: A flashing red light means the same as a stop sign. You must come to a complete stop, check for cross traffic and pedestrians, and proceed only when it is safe. A steady yellow or yellow arrow warns that the signal is about to turn red; you should prepare to stop if you can do so safely, but an immediate stop is not always required.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you hear or see an approaching emergency vehicle while on a divided multilane highway, you should:
options: a:Ignore it if other lanes exist for it to use,b:Stop immediately in your lane,c:Slow, move to provide a clear path, and stop,d:Speed up to get out of its way
note: When an emergency vehicle with lights and siren approaches, you must yield the right-of-way. On a divided multilane highway, slow down, move as far as you safely can to clear a path (usually to the right), and stop until the vehicle has passed. Do not speed up or stop suddenly in the middle of the lane without creating a clear path.

question: Approaching a railroad crossing with no flashing lights or gates, what should you do?
options: a:Be prepared to yield to any train at the crossing.,b:Always stop before crossing the tracks.,c:Cross the tracks immediately and as quickly as possible.
note: At a railroad crossing without lights or gates, you must approach with caution: slow down, look and listen for trains, and be prepared to stop. You must yield to any train in or near the crossing and never enter the tracks unless there is enough space for your entire vehicle to clear the tracks on the far side.

question: When approaching a blind pedestrian using a white cane or guide dog, you should:
options: a:Slow down and be prepared to stop, yielding the right-of-way.,b:Take the right-of-way.,c:Proceed normally at the same speed.
note: Blind pedestrians using a white cane or guide dog have the right-of-way. You must slow down, be prepared to stop, and yield so they can cross safely. Do not honk or try to force your way through; give them extra time and space.

question: What is the most common cause of traffic crashes?
options: a:New drivers,b:Bad weather,c:Human error
note: Most traffic crashes are caused by human error, such as inattention, distraction, following too closely, speeding, or failing to yield. While bad weather and road conditions can contribute, driver decisions and mistakes are the primary cause of most collisions.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When you approach an intersection with a flashing red light, you should:
options: a:Come to a full stop, then proceed when it is safe.,b:Slow down and proceed without stopping.,c:Only stop if other cars are also approaching.
note: A flashing red light is treated the same as a stop sign. You must come to a complete stop, check for cross traffic and pedestrians, yield the right‑of‑way as needed, and then proceed only when it is safe.

question: If you hit a parked, unattended vehicle and cannot find the owner, what must you do?
options: a:Must leave a written notice containing your name, your address, and the circumstances of the accident.,b:Must stay until the police arrive.,c:Have done as much as you can.
note: If you hit a parked vehicle and cannot find the owner, you are legally required to leave a written note with your name, address, and an explanation of what happened, and securely attach it to the vehicle. You should also report the collision as required by local law.

question: How is distracted driving best described?
options: a:Nothing to be concerned about.,b:Very uncommon.,c:Extremely risky behavior.
note: Distracted driving is extremely dangerous because it takes your eyes, mind, or hands away from the driving task. It greatly increases the risk of crashes and can harm you, your passengers, and others on the road.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: How should you check your blind spot before changing lanes?
options: a:Look into the rearview mirror.,b:Look into the side mirror.,c:Look over your shoulder into the blind spot you plan to enter.
note: Before changing lanes, you must briefly look over your shoulder in the direction you plan to move. This head check lets you see the blind spot that your mirrors cannot cover, helping you avoid vehicles riding alongside you.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When you see an emergency vehicle with flashing lights approaching, what must you do?
options: a:Slow down and keep moving in your lane.,b:Keep driving in your lane.,c:Pull to the right curb and stop.
note: When an emergency vehicle approaches with flashing lights or a siren, you must yield the right‑of‑way by pulling as far to the right as safely possible and stopping. Stay stopped until the emergency vehicle has passed, unless directed otherwise by officials.

question: If a train is close enough or fast enough to be a danger, you must do what?
options: a:Slow down and proceed with caution,b:Cross the tracks at your own risk,c:Not cross until the train has completely passed,d:Wave to the engineer
note: If a train is close enough or moving fast enough to pose any danger, you must stop and wait. Do not try to beat the train; stay back until the train has completely passed and you can clearly see that the tracks are clear in both directions.

question: If you drink socially, which strategy helps ensure you do not drive impaired?
options: a:Take a cold shower before driving.,b:Drink coffee before driving.,c:Ride home with a friend who has not been drinking.
note: Arrange a sober ride home; coffee or a cold shower do not reduce blood alcohol content or impairment.

question: When may you legally cross double solid yellow lines?
options: a:To pass a slow-moving truck.,b:To turn into a driveway or make a left turn where permitted.,c:To pass another car.
note: Double solid yellow lines separate traffic moving in opposite directions and mean no passing. However, you may carefully cross them to turn left into or out of a driveway, side road, or alley, or to make a legal U‑turn when it is safe and not otherwise prohibited.

question: An octagonal (eight-sided) traffic sign always means:
options: a:A speed limit sign.,b:A stop sign.,c:A hospital sign.
note: An eight‑sided (octagonal) sign is used only for STOP signs. When you see this shape, you must come to a complete stop at the limit line, crosswalk, or before entering the intersection, and proceed only when it is safe.

question: When is it important to slow down?
options: a:On narrow or winding roads,b:At intersections or railroad crossings,c:When the road is wet or slippery,d:All of the above
note: You should reduce speed whenever conditions increase risk: on narrow or winding roads, near intersections and railroad crossings where hazards may appear suddenly, and on wet or slippery roads where stopping distance is longer and traction is reduced.

question: As you approach an accident scene, what should you do if you are not involved?
options: a:Stop and go look at the crash.,b:Keep your attention on driving and continue moving unless you are involved or emergency help has not yet arrived.,c:Get out of your car to help even if others are already assisting.
note: If you are not involved in a crash, do not stop just to look. This creates additional hazards and can cause more collisions. Continue driving, stay alert for people or vehicles in the roadway, and only stop if you are directly involved or if emergency help is clearly needed and has not yet arrived.

question: Which statement about passing a motorcycle is correct?
options: a:It is okay for other vehicles to follow motorcycles closely.,b:A motorcycle with two people is more balanced than one with a single rider.,c:The driver of a passenger vehicle must change lanes completely when passing a motorcycle.
note: Motorcycles are entitled to a full lane, just like any other vehicle. When passing, you must move completely into the adjacent lane and give the motorcycle plenty of space. Do not crowd or share the lane with a motorcycle, and never follow one too closely because they can stop or maneuver more quickly than a car.

question: Which is NOT a factor in determining stopping distance?
options: a:Reaction distance,b:Braking distance,c:Steering ability,d:Perception time
note: Total stopping distance is made up of perception time (seeing and recognizing a hazard), reaction distance (the distance traveled while you move your foot to the brake), and braking distance (the distance it takes to stop after braking begins). Steering ability does not directly determine how far it takes to stop.

question: When driving near a motorcycle, you must:
options: a:Allow the motorcycle a full travel lane,b:Share half of your lane with the motorcycle,c:Drive on the shoulder beside the motorcycle,d:Require the motorcyclist to ride to the right edge
note: A motorcycle uses the full width of a lane and must be given the same space as a car. Do not try to share a lane side‑by‑side with a motorcycle, drive on the shoulder next to it, or force it to the edge of the lane. Always allow the motorcycle a complete travel lane.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Drivers may not pass from either side of which centerline marking?
options: a:Single broken yellow line.,b:Combination broken and solid yellow line.,c:Double solid yellow line.
note: A double solid yellow centerline means no passing is allowed for traffic in either direction. You may cross it only when making a permitted left turn or entering/exiting a driveway or side road, but you may not use it to pass another vehicle from either side.

question: Sections of road shaded by trees or buildings often freeze more quickly when roads are:
options: a:In the sun,b:Curvy,c:Flat,d:Shaded
note: Shaded sections of road freeze first and thaw last compared with nearby areas that are in the sun. When the rest of the road is exposed to sunlight, it may look wet or clear while shaded patches can still be icy and very slippery, so you must slow down and be especially cautious when moving from sunny pavement into shaded areas.

question: Which driving habit helps conserve gasoline?
options: a:Accelerating quickly.,b:Sitting in your driveway with the car running.,c:Slowing down gradually and avoiding unnecessary braking.
note: Looking well ahead and slowing down gradually helps you avoid unnecessary braking and rapid acceleration, both of which waste fuel. Smooth, steady driving with fewer hard starts and stops improves gas mileage and reduces wear on your vehicle.

question: What is the most common color of warning signs?
options: a:Green,b:Red,c:Yellow,d:Blue
note: Most general warning signs in the United States are diamond-shaped and yellow with black symbols or lettering. These signs alert you to conditions such as curves, intersections, pedestrian crossings, or other potential hazards ahead so you can adjust your driving in time.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When should you use your turn signal?
options: a:Only when other traffic is present.,b:Only during the maneuver, not before.,c:Whenever you change lanes, pull into or out of a parking space, or pull into traffic from a parking area or alley.
note: You should always signal before you change lanes, turn, enter or leave a parking space, or pull into traffic from a curb, driveway, or alley. Signaling early and clearly lets other road users know what you intend to do so they can adjust their speed or position safely.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you are stopped in a line of vehicles at a stop sign and there is no cross traffic after the vehicles ahead proceed, what should you do?
options: a:May proceed through the intersection without stopping again.,b:May slowly roll past the stop sign.,c:Must stop again at the stop sign or stop line before proceeding.
note: Each driver must make a complete stop at the stop sign or stop line, even if the vehicles ahead have already stopped and gone. After stopping, you must yield to any pedestrians and cross traffic before you proceed through the intersection.

question: As you approach an intersection and the light turns from green to yellow, what should you do?
options: a:Apply the brakes sharply to stop.,b:Be prepared to stop.,c:Speed up to beat the red light.
note: A steady yellow light warns that the signal is about to turn red. You should slow down and be prepared to stop if you can do so safely, rather than speeding up to get through the intersection.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you miss your exit on a freeway, what should you do?
options: a:Stop and back up,b:Make the turn quickly from your lane,c:Continue to the next exit where you can safely turn around,d:Pull onto the shoulder and reverse
note: If you miss your exit on a freeway, stay calm and continue driving to the next exit. It is illegal and extremely dangerous to stop, back up, or reverse on the freeway or shoulder to try to reach a missed exit.

question: How close to a fire hydrant may you legally park?
options: a:10 feet,b:15 feet,c:25 feet
note: You must not park too close to a fire hydrant so firefighters have clear access in an emergency. In many states the minimum distance is 15 feet, though some local laws may differ. Always check your state’s specific parking distance requirements.

question: If someone is injured in an accident you are involved in, what should you do?
options: a:Not move the injured unnecessarily; keep them warm and administer first aid.,b:Move the injured away from the scene immediately.,c:Always leave the injured where they are.
note: If someone is injured, call emergency services and do not move them unless there is immediate danger, such as fire or traffic. Keep the person warm, reassure them, and give first aid only if you are trained, while waiting for professional help.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which of the following is a safe condition to pass another vehicle?
options: a:When you are on a hill or in a curve and cannot see ahead.,b:If your lane is next to a broken yellow line and the opposing lane is clear.,c:By driving onto the shoulder of the highway.
note: You may pass another vehicle only when the center line on your side is a broken yellow line and the opposing lane is clear of oncoming traffic. Never pass on hills, curves where you cannot see far enough ahead, or by driving on the shoulder.

question: You must stop at a railroad crossing when which condition exists?
options: a:Directed by a flagger,b:A stop sign controls the crossing,c:Flashing red signals and gates are operating,d:Any of the above
note: You must stop at a railroad crossing any time a flagger directs you to stop, a stop sign controls the crossing, or flashing red lights and/or gates are operating. These controls indicate that a train may be approaching or the crossing is otherwise unsafe to enter.

question: Before changing lanes, what should you do?
options: a:Signal your intention ahead of the lane change,b:Check your blind spot,c:Ensure the lane is clear before moving,d:All of the above
note: Before changing lanes, always signal in advance to communicate your intentions, check your mirrors and blind spots to see vehicles you cannot see directly, and make sure the lane is clear and safe before moving over.

question: When should you drive below the posted speed limit?
options: a:Whenever conditions are less than ideal, such as bad weather, poor visibility, or heavy traffic.,b:Only when entering a highway where there are other cars.,c:Whenever you see a police car, even if conditions are normal.
note: You must slow below the posted speed limit whenever conditions are less than ideal—such as rain, snow, fog, heavy traffic, sharp curves, or poor visibility. The basic speed law requires you to drive at a speed that is safe for current conditions, and you can be cited for driving too fast for conditions even if you are under the posted limit.

question: Which of the following influence your blood alcohol concentration (BAC)?
options: a:The amount of food in your stomach and how much time passes between drinks.,b:Your body weight.,c:All of the above, along with how much alcohol you drink.
note: Your blood alcohol concentration (BAC) is affected by how much alcohol you drink, how quickly you drink it, your body weight, and whether you have food in your stomach. Food and body weight may slow the rate at which alcohol enters your bloodstream, but they do not prevent impairment or make it safe to drink and drive.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When entering a street from a driveway, you must:
options: a:Yield to any approaching vehicles or pedestrians after coming to a stop,b:Honk your horn to warn approaching vehicles,c:Drive slowly without stopping,d:Enter without regard to oncoming traffic
note: When entering a street from a driveway or alley, you must stop before the sidewalk or edge of the roadway, yield to pedestrians on the sidewalk and to all approaching vehicles, and only proceed when it is safe. You must not enter the roadway without stopping and yielding.

question: If your vehicle's accelerator sticks open while driving, what general steps should you take?
options: a:Blow your horn repeatedly.,b:Turn off the ignition immediately without caution.,c:Turn the ignition off carefully if needed, apply brakes, and move off the road to a safe area.
note: If the accelerator sticks, keep calm, shift to neutral if possible, and steer straight. Apply the brakes firmly and steadily, then carefully turn the ignition off without locking the steering. Signal and steer to the side of the road and stop in a safe place.

question: How should young children be secured in a vehicle to be safest?
options: a:May be safely held by a strong adult.,b:May stand on the floor in the back of the vehicle.,c:Be properly restrained in a child seat or appropriate safety belt.
note: Young children must always be in an appropriate child safety seat or properly fitted safety belt, never held in someone’s arms or allowed to stand. In a crash, an adult cannot hold onto a child against the force of impact, so proper restraints are essential.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When may you legally cross a solid yellow line?
options: a:To pass traffic moving in the same direction.,b:To make a turn into a driveway or side street.,c:During daylight hours only.
note: A solid yellow line generally means no passing, but you may cross it when you are turning left into or out of a driveway, alley, or side street, as long as it is safe and legal to do so. You may not cross it just to pass another vehicle.

question: How can you reduce the chance of hydroplaning?
options: a:Replace tires with good tread, maintain correct tire pressure, and avoid speeding on wet roads.,b:Drive faster to rise above the water.,c:Use low tire pressure intentionally.
note: Hydroplaning happens when your tires ride on top of water and lose contact with the road. To reduce the risk, keep your tires properly inflated, replace them when the tread is worn, and slow down on wet roads—especially in heavy rain or standing water.

question: Which of these actions can cause distracted driving?
options: a:Eating, drinking, or smoking while driving,b:Changing a radio station or CD,c:Talking or texting on a cell phone,d:Any of the above
note: Any activity that takes your eyes, hands, or mind away from driving is a distraction. Eating, adjusting the radio, and especially talking or texting on a phone all reduce your attention to the road and increase the chance of a crash.

question: Which substances may impair driving and could lead to a DUII arrest?
options: a:Beer, wine, and other liquor,b:Controlled or illegal drugs and some prescription medicines,c:Inhalants like glue or paint,d:All of the above
note: Alcohol, illegal drugs, many prescription medications, and inhalants can all affect judgment, reaction time, and coordination. Any substance that impairs your ability to drive safely can lead to a DUII arrest, even if it is legally prescribed or purchased.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: On which traffic signal do you have the right-of-way to turn left?
options: a:A flashing yellow light.,b:A solid green light.,c:A green arrow pointing left.
note: A steady green arrow for a left turn means you have a protected turn: oncoming traffic and pedestrians should be stopped, and you have the right-of-way to turn left when it is safe. A solid green light or flashing yellow may allow a left turn, but you must yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians.

question: When the centerline shows a solid yellow next to a broken yellow line with the broken line next to your lane, when may you pass?
options: a:Only in an emergency.,b:If traffic is clear and it is safe.,c:If you are on an expressway.
note: A broken yellow line next to your lane means you may pass if it is safe and there is no oncoming traffic. The solid yellow line on the other side means vehicles in that lane may not pass. Always be sure you have enough clear distance ahead before crossing the centerline.
