question: If an approaching driver fails to dim their high beams, where should you look?
options: a:At the wheels of the approaching vehicle.,b:Toward the right side of the road.,c:Toward the left side of the road.
note: When another driver does not dim their high beams, look toward the right edge of your lane or the right side of the road. This reduces glare while still letting you use the road edge and lane markings to stay in your lane until the vehicle passes.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: On a two-way, two-lane road, you cannot pass safely unless which condition is met?
options: a:You are able to clearly see the road ahead,b:You can return to your lane before meeting oncoming traffic,c:Your vehicle can reach the speed necessary to pass,d:All of the above
note: Safe passing on a two-way, two-lane road requires all three conditions: you must clearly see far enough ahead, have enough space to return to your lane before meeting oncoming traffic, and your vehicle must be able to accelerate and complete the pass without forcing others to slow or swerve.

question: While backing, what is the recommended practice?
options: a:Turn your head and look through the rear window while backing,b:Rely only on mirrors,c:Open the door and look out while backing,d:Flash your lights before reversing
note: When backing, you should turn your head and look directly through the rear window so you can clearly see the path behind you. Mirrors and cameras can help, but they have blind spots and should not be your only source of information.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When a traffic signal displays a steady green arrow, what does that mean?
options: a:You must stop and wait.,b:You may turn in the arrow's direction after yielding to pedestrians and traffic already in the intersection.,c:You have no responsibility to yield to pedestrians.
note: A steady green arrow means you are allowed to turn in the direction of the arrow, usually with a protected turn. You must still yield to pedestrians in the crosswalk and any vehicles already in the intersection before completing your turn.

question: What should you do when driving to an unfamiliar area?
options: a:Depend only on road signs to find your way.,b:Plan your route in advance.,c:Only have a general idea of where you are going.
note: Before driving into an unfamiliar area, you should plan your route in advance. Reviewing maps or navigation directions ahead of time reduces last‑second lane changes, missed turns, and distracted driving while you try to figure out where to go.

question: What does a single dashed yellow centerline indicate?
options: a:Drivers may pass if it is safe to do so,b:Both lanes travel in the same direction,c:Drivers may not pass,d:Only buses may pass
note: A single dashed yellow centerline separates traffic moving in opposite directions and allows passing in either direction when it is safe and legal. You must still check for oncoming traffic and ensure you have enough clear distance to pass safely.

question: What does a flashing yellow traffic light instruct drivers to do?
options: a:Stop immediately,b:Proceed with caution,c:Yield to pedestrians only,d:Turn only when signaled
note: A flashing yellow traffic light means slow down and proceed with caution. You do not have to stop, but you must be prepared to yield if necessary and carefully check for cross traffic, pedestrians, or other hazards.

question: How does increasing your vehicle’s speed affect your field of vision?
options: a:Increases your field of vision.,b:Decreases your field of vision.,c:Makes it easier to see cross traffic.
note: As speed increases, your field of vision narrows and you see less to the sides. This is why higher speeds require extra caution and scanning, because you have less time and a smaller visual area to detect hazards.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If two vehicles reach an uncontrolled intersection simultaneously, which one must yield?
options: a:The largest vehicle,b:The car on the left,c:The car on the left must yield to the car on the right,d:The car on the right must yield
note: At an uncontrolled intersection where two vehicles arrive at the same time, the driver on the left must yield to the driver on the right. This right‑of‑way rule helps prevent confusion and collisions when there are no signs or signals.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When a stop is required at an intersection that has no stop line or crosswalk, where should you stop?
options: a:Slow down to make sure crossing traffic is clear.,b:Stop at the point nearest the intersecting roadway where you can see approaching traffic.,c:You are not required to stop.
note: If there is no stop line or crosswalk, you must stop before entering the intersection at the point nearest the intersecting roadway where you can clearly see approaching traffic. Do not pull into the intersection to get a better view before stopping.

question: How should a seat belt fit when properly adjusted?
options: a:Is loose across your hip bones.,b:Is buckled snugly across your hip bones (low on the hips, not the stomach).,c:Is hidden beneath the seat.
note: A lap belt should be snug across the hip bones, not the stomach, to spread crash forces over the stronger pelvic bones. The shoulder belt should cross the center of the chest and shoulder, not the neck or face, and should lie flat without slack.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When preparing to turn left, what should you do?
options: a:Signal and watch for oncoming vehicles and pedestrians.,b:Speed up to clear the intersection faster.,c:Turn into any available lane.
note: Before turning left, signal well in advance, check mirrors and blind spots, and move into the correct lane. Yield to oncoming traffic, pedestrians, and cyclists, and only turn when it is safe and legal to do so.

question: When driving in fog, you should use which lights?
options: a:High beam headlights,b:Low beam headlights,c:Parking lights only,d:Interior dome light
note: Use low beam headlights in fog because their light aims down toward the road and reduces glare. High beams reflect off the water droplets in fog and can actually make it harder to see. If your vehicle has fog lights, use them with your low beams for better visibility.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When preparing to make a right turn, where should your car be positioned?
options: a:Near the center of the street,b:Close to the left side of the street,c:Close to the right side of the street,d:Centered in your lane regardless of direction
note: Before a right turn, you should move your vehicle as close as safely possible to the right edge or curb. This positioning clearly signals your intention, shortens the turn, and prevents other drivers from trying to pass you on the right.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What is the correct action if you find yourself stopped in a travel lane?
options: a:Stop to drop off passengers.,b:Make a U-turn or back up if you miss an exit.,c:Keep moving until you can safely pull off the road; do not stop in a travel lane.
note: You should not stop in a travel lane unless it is an emergency or traffic requires it. If you miss an exit or turn, keep driving until you can safely leave the roadway or turn around; never back up or make a U-turn from a travel lane.

question: When you hear the siren of a fire engine behind you, what must you do?
options: a:Slow down until it passes you.,b:Drive with your flashers on.,c:Pull over to the side of the road and stop to let it pass.
note: When an emergency vehicle using sirens and flashing lights approaches, you must yield the right-of-way by pulling over to the right side of the road and stopping, when safe. Stay stopped until the vehicle has passed and it is safe to re-enter traffic.

question: To prepare for hazards ahead on the road, you should do what?
options: a:Continuously scan the entire roadway and roadsides,b:Stare straight ahead at all times,c:Drive with your foot lightly on the brake,d:Focus only on the vehicle immediately ahead
note: To spot hazards early, keep your eyes moving and scan the road ahead, to the sides, and in your mirrors. Looking far ahead and not staring at one spot gives you more time to react to changing traffic, pedestrians, and road conditions.

question: When an emergency vehicle is approaching with flashing red or blue lights, what should you do?
options: a:Continue driving but try to stay out of its way.,b:See if you can reach your destination first.,c:Pull over to the side of the road and come to a complete stop when safe.
note: When an emergency vehicle approaches using lights and siren, you must yield the right-of-way. Safely pull over to the right side of the road and come to a complete stop until the vehicle has passed, unless directed otherwise by law enforcement or it is unsafe to do so.

question: How do you check your vehicle's blind spots?
options: a:By looking in your side mirrors.,b:By turning your head and looking over your shoulder.,c:By looking in your rearview mirror.
note: Blind spots are areas you cannot see with your mirrors alone. Before changing lanes or merging, quickly turn your head and look over the shoulder in the direction you intend to move to be sure no vehicle is in your blind spot.

question: Where is it best to maintain a space cushion around your vehicle?
options: a:Only behind your vehicle.,b:On all sides of your vehicle.,c:Only in front of your vehicle.
note: A space cushion is a safety margin around your vehicle. Keeping space in front, behind, and to both sides gives you time and room to react if another driver makes a mistake or traffic suddenly slows or stops.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: To check your blind spot before changing lanes to the left you should glance:
options: a:At your side mirror.,b:Over your left shoulder.,c:Over your right shoulder.
note: Before moving into the lane to your left, check your mirrors and then glance over your left shoulder. This quick head check lets you see the left-side blind spot that your mirrors cannot show.

question: What lane entitlement do motorcycles have on the road?
options: a:The bicycle lane.,b:The same full lane width as other motor vehicles.,c:Half the width of a lane.
note: Motorcycles are entitled to use a full traffic lane, just like cars and trucks. Do not crowd them or share their lane; give them the same space and respect you would give any other motor vehicle.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When entering a highway from an entrance ramp, what is the usual merging procedure?
options: a:Use the acceleration lane to reach the speed of traffic and merge when safe.,b:Stop at the end of the ramp, then slowly enter.,c:Enter well below the speed of traffic to be cautious.
note: Use the acceleration lane to increase speed to match traffic, signal, check mirrors and blind spots, and merge when safe.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When making a right turn on a steady green light, what must you do?
options: a:Maintain your normal driving speed.,b:Yield to pedestrians.,c:Stop and look for nearby police cars.
note: You may turn on a steady green unless a sign prohibits it, but you must yield to pedestrians and any traffic with the right-of-way before turning.

question: What effect does eating or drinking while driving usually have on vehicle control?
options: a:Have trouble maintaining proper vehicle control and lane position.,b:Make no driving errors.,c:Are better drivers because they are not hungry.
note: Eating or drinking while driving is distracting: it takes hands off the wheel and eyes off the road, increasing the likelihood of lane drift and control errors.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Unless otherwise posted, what is the maximum speed limit on a dirt or gravel road?
options: a:20 mph,b:40 mph,c:55 mph,d:35 mph
note: On unpaved dirt or gravel roads, you must drive more slowly because traction is reduced and stopping distances are longer. Many states set a lower default speed limit for these roads, commonly around 35 mph unless otherwise posted. Always adjust your speed further for visibility, curves, hills, and traffic conditions.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: You are required to stop your vehicle under which of the following circumstances?
options: a:At an intersection with a stop sign, at a red light, or when a traffic officer orders you to stop.,b:Only when a traffic officer orders you to stop.,c:Only at a stop sign.
note: You must stop at stop signs, red lights (including flashing red), and whenever a traffic officer directs you to stop.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What does a posted speed limit sign indicate?
options: a:The exact safe speed to avoid a ticket regardless of conditions.,b:The maximum legal speed under ideal conditions.,c:Only a recommended driving speed.
note: A posted speed limit is the maximum legal speed allowed on that road in ideal conditions. You must slow down below the limit when conditions are poor, such as in rain, fog, heavy traffic, or construction zones.

question: If you are taking a non-prescription drug, what should you do before driving?
options: a:Read the labels on the medication and heed any warnings about driving.,b:Drink alcohol instead to counteract side effects.,c:Continue to drive regardless of any warning labels.
note: Many over‑the‑counter medicines can make you drowsy, dizzy, or otherwise impair your driving. Always read the label and follow any driving warnings, and ask a doctor or pharmacist if you are unsure whether it is safe to drive.

question: Which actions help you drive safely at night?
options: a:Make sure headlights are working properly, not drive if tired, and increase your following distance.,b:Drive only with parking lights.,c:Keep your windshield dirty to reduce glare.
note: Safe night driving requires good visibility and extra caution. Make sure your headlights and other lights work properly, avoid driving when you are tired, and increase your following distance because it is harder to see hazards and judge distances in the dark.

question: Blood alcohol concentration (BAC) is affected by all of the following except:
options: a:How much time passes between drinks.,b:Your body weight.,c:The type of alcoholic beverage consumed.
note: BAC depends on how much alcohol you consume, how quickly you drink it, your body weight, and how much time passes as your body processes the alcohol. A standard amount of alcohol has a similar effect on BAC whether it is in beer, wine, or liquor; the type of drink matters only because it changes how much alcohol you take in, not how your body processes it.

question: Which practice helps prevent rear-end collisions when stopping?
options: a:Release the gas pedal and let your vehicle slow before applying the brakes.,b:Avoid sudden stops.,c:Before stopping, check your mirrors for traffic behind you and brake gradually when possible.
note: To reduce the risk of being hit from behind, you should avoid sudden stops by slowing gradually and signaling early, and you should check your mirrors before braking so you know how close vehicles are behind you. Easing off the gas to slow before braking can help, but it is only one part of safe stopping and is not the single best answer by itself.

question: When roads may be slippery, what should you avoid doing?
options: a:Always driving at the maximum speed limit.,b:Using cruise control to maintain a steady speed.,c:Making sudden changes in speed or direction; instead reduce speed and increase following distance.
note: On slippery roads you should slow down, avoid sudden steering, braking, or acceleration, increase your following distance, and never use cruise control. Cruise control can cause your wheels to spin faster if you start to skid, making it harder to regain control. Smooth, gentle inputs and extra space are key to staying safe on wet, icy, or snowy pavement.

question: Which of the following is a common effect of drinking alcohol while driving?
options: a:Your judgment of speed and distance is distorted.,b:You become more alert and reactive.,c:Your reflexes improve.
note: Alcohol affects the brain areas that control judgment, coordination, and vision. Even small amounts can distort your sense of speed and distance, slow your reaction time, and reduce alertness. Because of this, you are less able to judge gaps, follow at a safe distance, or react quickly to hazards, which greatly increases crash risk.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: You arrive at a 4-way stop at the same time as a driver on your left. Who has the right of way?
options: a:The driver on your left, because they were there first,b:You have the right of way — the driver to your left must yield to you,c:Whoever signals first proceeds first,d:The driver going straight always has priority
note: At a 4-way stop when two vehicles arrive simultaneously, the driver to the RIGHT has the right of way. Since the other driver is to your LEFT, you are to their right — meaning you have the right of way and should proceed first.

question: If you must make an emergency stop on an interstate, what should you do?
options: a:Get out of your vehicle and flag down the first vehicle that passes.,b:Pull off the road, turn on your emergency flashers, and stay in your vehicle, if you can.,c:Sound your horn at passing cars to get their attention.
note: If you must stop on an interstate, pull completely off the travel lanes onto the shoulder if possible, turn on your emergency flashers so others can see you, and stay inside your vehicle with your seat belt fastened unless there is an immediate danger such as fire or traffic striking your vehicle.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When preparing to pass on a two-lane road, what should be your primary check?
options: a:Judge the distance and speed of oncoming vehicles.,b:Flash your headlights as you pass.,c:Sound your horn as you pass.,d:Assume oncoming traffic will slow down.
note: Before passing on a two-lane road, your main concern is whether there is enough clear space ahead in the oncoming lane. Carefully judge the distance and speed of oncoming vehicles and only begin passing if you are sure you can complete the maneuver and return to your lane without forcing any other driver to slow or swerve.

question: On which road marking may you legally pass another vehicle?
options: a:You are on a road with a solid line next to your lane.,b:You are on a hill or curve.,c:You are on a road with a broken line next to your lane.
note: A broken center line next to your lane means you may pass when it is safe. A solid line next to your lane means you must not pass, and you should never pass on hills, curves, or anywhere your view of oncoming traffic is limited.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: After passing another vehicle, you should move back into your original lane when:
options: a:You have cleared the front bumper of the passed vehicle.,b:You can see the passed vehicle’s headlights in your rearview mirror.,c:You are 50 feet ahead of the passed vehicle.,d:The passing vehicle signals you to move over.
note: After passing, do not move back into your original lane until you can see the front of the vehicle you passed (its headlights in the daytime or at night) in your rearview mirror. This ensures you have enough space ahead and do not cut off the other driver.

question: What do blue traffic signs generally indicate?
options: a:Regulatory requirements like speed limits.,b:Mileage distances to locations.,c:Construction and maintenance warnings.,d:Information on motorist services (rest areas, hospitals, food).
note: Blue traffic signs are service signs. They give information about motorist services such as rest areas, gas stations, food, lodging, and hospitals along the roadway.

question: When entering a freeway, how should you check traffic to merge safely?
options: a:Using your side mirror and looking over your shoulder.,b:Using only your rearview mirror.,c:Using your rearview and side mirrors without looking over your shoulder.
note: Before merging onto a freeway, use your mirrors and then look over your shoulder to check your blind spot. This helps you see vehicles that are not visible in your mirrors so you can choose a safe gap and merge smoothly.

question: If a child is about to run into the street, what should you do?
options: a:Sound a sharp blast of your horn while being prepared to stop.,b:Flash your headlights.,c:Continue at the same speed.
note: If a child appears ready to run into the street, immediately cover the brake and be prepared to stop while giving a sharp blast of your horn to warn the child and others nearby. Use the horn to alert, but your primary responsibility is to slow or stop to avoid a collision.

question: What must you do when approaching a pedestrian who uses a guide dog or white cane?
options: a:Honk so they know to clear the way.,b:Swerve quickly around them.,c:Yield the right-of-way.
note: Stop and give the blind pedestrian the right-of-way; do not honk or attempt to steer around them abruptly.

question: Alcohol is classified as which type of substance?
options: a:A depressant.,b:A stimulant.,c:An antihistamine.
note: Alcohol is a central nervous system depressant. It slows brain activity and impairs judgment, coordination, and reaction time, making it dangerous to drive after drinking.

question: Any amount of alcohol in your blood may affect which abilities?
options: a:Right-of-way privileges.,b:Judgment and physical coordination.,c:Knowledge.
note: Any amount of alcohol can affect your judgment and physical coordination, even if you do not feel drunk. Because driving requires quick decisions and precise control, even small amounts of alcohol can make driving unsafe.

question: When is using your horn appropriate?
options: a:When it may help prevent a collision.,b:When another driver makes a mistake.,c:When another vehicle is in your way and you want them to move.
note: Use your horn only to alert others to a potential collision or to warn of immediate danger. Do not use it to show anger, impatience, or to punish other drivers for mistakes.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Where is it safe to pass another vehicle?
options: a:Where signs and pavement markings indicate passing is permitted and it is safe.,b:Within an intersection if no oncoming vehicles are present.,c:On a curve if you can see ahead a short distance.,d:Anywhere if you signal before passing.
note: Passing is only safe and legal where signs and pavement markings allow it and you have enough clear space to pass without speeding or cutting back in too closely. Never pass in intersections, on curves, or where your view is blocked by hills or other obstacles.

question: At a crosswalk, who has the right-of-way?
options: a:Construction workers must yield to you.,b:You must yield to pedestrians.,c:Pedestrians must yield to you.
note: Drivers must yield to pedestrians in crosswalks, whether marked or unmarked, when pedestrians are in or approaching your lane. Always be prepared to stop for people crossing the street.

question: What does a green arrow signal require you to do?
options: a:Proceed immediately without yielding.,b:Ignore any pedestrians in the intersection.,c:Wait four seconds before proceeding.,d:Yield to vehicles, bicyclists, and pedestrians in the intersection, then complete the turn.
note: A green arrow gives you a protected movement in the direction of the arrow, but you must still yield to any vehicles, bicyclists, or pedestrians already in the intersection before you complete your turn.

question: Why is winter driving more hazardous than other seasons?
options: a:There are increased hours of darkness.,b:Road conditions can be affected by freezing temperatures, ice, snow, and fog.,c:Both of the above.
note: Winter driving is more dangerous because there are more hours of darkness and road surfaces can become slippery or obscured by ice, snow, and fog. These conditions reduce traction and visibility, requiring slower speeds and greater following distances.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What general attitude should a driver have about right-of-way rules?
options: a:Assume most drivers obey the right-of-way rules.,b:Always be prepared to yield the right-of-way.,c:Assume all drivers automatically obey the right-of-way rules.
note: Right-of-way laws say who should go first, but they do not guarantee that others will follow them. Safe drivers always stay ready to yield, even when they legally have the right-of-way, if yielding will prevent a collision.

question: When you see a school crossing sign, what should you do?
options: a:Always sound your horn when you see children.,b:Watch for children and be ready to stop.,c:Always stop, whether there is a stop sign or not.
note: A school crossing sign warns that children may be crossing the road. You should slow down, scan carefully for children, and be prepared to stop if they are in or near the crosswalk. You do not automatically stop unless required by a stop sign, signal, or pedestrians in the crosswalk.

question: If a tire blows out suddenly while you're driving, what steps should you take?
options: a:Hold the steering wheel firmly, ease off the accelerator, and exit the traffic lane slowly.,b:Pump the brakes rapidly to stop quickly.,c:Brake hard and steer immediately to the right edge.,d:Turn on your hazards and speed up to reach the shoulder faster.
note: When a tire blows out, the car may pull to one side. Hold the steering wheel firmly, ease off the accelerator, and let the vehicle slow down. Once it is under control and speed has dropped, steer gradually off the road and brake gently if needed. Sudden hard braking or sharp steering can cause loss of control.

question: How many alcoholic drinks does it take to affect your driving ability?
options: a:One,b:Two,c:Three
note: Alcohol begins to affect judgment and reaction time with the first drink. Even one drink can impair your ability to drive safely, so the safest choice is not to drive after drinking any amount of alcohol.

question: What is the only thing that can reduce blood alcohol concentration (BAC)?
options: a:Time,b:Eating foods high in fat,c:Drinking caffeine
note: Once alcohol is in your system, only time allows your body to metabolize it and lower your BAC. Food, coffee, cold showers, or exercise may make you feel more awake but do not speed up the elimination of alcohol.

question: When ridden on public roadways, bicycles are legally classified as:
options: a:Pedestrians.,b:Vehicles.,c:Hazards.,d:Motor vehicles.
note: Bicycles ridden on public roads are treated as vehicles. Cyclists must obey traffic signals, signs, lane markings, and right‑of‑way rules just like drivers of cars, including stopping at red lights and stop signs and riding in the same direction as traffic.

question: If your vehicle has a two-part seat belt, how should you wear it?
options: a:Use only the shoulder belt.,b:Use both the lap and shoulder belts.,c:Use only the lap belt.
note: If your vehicle has both a lap belt and a shoulder belt, you must wear both. The lap belt should be low and snug across the hips, and the shoulder belt should cross the chest and shoulder, not the neck or under the arm. Using only one part greatly reduces protection in a crash.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Where is a U-turn prohibited?
options: a:On a straight roadway with a clear view for 500 feet in both directions.,b:On or near any curve or hill.,c:In a parking lot.
note: You must not make a U‑turn on or near a curve or hill where you cannot see far enough ahead to be sure it is safe. Limited visibility makes it hard to judge oncoming traffic and can lead to serious head‑on collisions.

question: Driving noticeably slower than surrounding traffic is:
options: a:Often a hazard because other drivers may become frustrated and try to pass you.,b:Appropriate if you don’t know the speed limit.,c:A good idea if the weather is bad, but you must not drive so slowly that you unnecessarily block or endanger other traffic.
note: Driving much slower than the normal flow of traffic can be dangerous because other drivers may not expect it and may make sudden or risky lane changes or passing maneuvers. You should generally travel at the speed of traffic (within the speed limit) and adjust your speed reasonably for conditions, such as bad weather, without becoming an unnecessary obstruction.

question: What qualifies as a driving distraction?
options: a:Anything that causes evasive action while driving.,b:Anything that takes your attention away from driving.,c:Anything that causes you to pay more attention to driving.
note: A driving distraction is anything that takes your attention away from the driving task—your eyes from the road, your mind from driving, or your hands from the wheel. Examples include texting, eating, adjusting controls, or focusing on passengers instead of traffic.

question: When following another vehicle at night, what headlight setting should you use?
options: a:Keep your headlights on the low beam setting.,b:Use your high beam headlights.,c:Use your high beam headlights until you are within 10 feet of the vehicle ahead.
note: Use low beam headlights when following another vehicle at night so you do not shine bright light into the driver’s mirrors and eyes. High beams can blind or distract the driver ahead, increasing the risk of a crash.

question: What does a double solid yellow centerline indicate?
options: a:Both lanes may pass.,b:The lane to the right may pass.,c:Neither lane may pass.
note: A double solid yellow centerline separates traffic moving in opposite directions and means passing is not allowed from either direction. You may cross these lines only to turn left into or out of a driveway or side road when it is safe.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When you want to change lanes, which action should you never do?
options: a:Move into another lane while within an intersection.,b:Check your blind spot by looking over your shoulder.,c:Check for other drivers moving into the same lane.
note: You should not change lanes while you are in an intersection because traffic movements are more complex and other drivers may not expect a lane change there. Instead, change lanes before or after the intersection, and always check mirrors, blind spots, and signal first.

question: If your wheels drop off the pavement edge, what should you do to re-enter safely?
options: a:Wait until it is safe to do so, then gradually re-enter the roadway.,b:Turn back onto the roadway immediately.,c:Stop.
note: If your wheels drop off the pavement, stay calm, ease off the accelerator, and keep a firm grip on the wheel. When traffic allows, gently steer back onto the pavement at a shallow angle. Do not jerk the wheel or brake hard, as that can cause you to lose control.

question: Which headlights should you use to improve visibility in rain or fog?
options: a:High beam headlights.,b:Low beam headlights.,c:Parking lights.
note: In rain, fog, snow, or sleet, use low beam headlights. High beams reflect off moisture in the air and can create glare, making it harder to see. Low beams help you see the road and help other drivers see you without excessive glare.

question: Which driving skills are impaired by alcohol or drug use?
options: a:Alertness.,b:Coordination.,c:Both of the above.
note: Alcohol and many drugs slow your reaction time and make it harder to stay alert and coordinate steering, braking, and acceleration. Because both alertness and coordination are affected, your overall ability to drive safely is reduced.

question: What is the law regarding posters and signs on car windows?
options: a:Are a fun way to personalize your vehicle.,b:Are prohibited by state law if they obstruct a driver's view of the road.,c:Are allowed only if they do not contain offensive language.
note: State law prohibits placing signs or materials on vehicle windows that obstruct the driver's clear view of the roadway.

question: A flashing yellow light at an intersection tells you to:
options: a:Slow down and proceed with caution.,b:Come to a complete stop as quickly as possible.,c:Stop and proceed only when the intersection is clear.
note: A flashing yellow light warns you to slow down and proceed through the intersection with caution. You do not have to stop unless needed for other traffic, pedestrians, or to avoid a hazard.

question: How do you drive defensively?
options: a:Put one car length between you and the car ahead.,b:Look only at the car in front of you while driving.,c:Keep your eyes moving to look for possible hazards.
note: Defensive driving means constantly scanning the road ahead, behind, and to the sides so you can spot potential hazards early. By keeping your eyes moving and checking mirrors, you have more time to react and avoid collisions.

question: Before switching on the ignition, what safety checks should you perform?
options: a:Be sure all passengers have buckled their safety belts.,b:Buckle your safety belt.,c:Both of the above.
note: Before starting the vehicle, you should always buckle your own seat belt and make sure all passengers are properly buckled. This simple habit greatly reduces the risk of injury in a crash.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: A pedestrian starts crossing after the \Don't Walk\" signal begins flashing and is in the middle of the street when your light turns green. What should you do?"
options: a:Proceed if the pedestrian is not in your lane.,b:Wait until the pedestrian finishes crossing before proceeding.,c:Proceed since you have the green and the pedestrian is mid-street.,d:Honk to make the pedestrian hurry.
note: If a pedestrian is in the intersection when your light turns green, allow them to finish crossing before you proceed.

question: You should avoid using your horn when driving near:
options: a:Drivers whose visibility ahead is limited.,b:Blind pedestrians.,c:Vehicles about to collide with you.,d:Pedestrians in crosswalks at night.
note: You should not use your horn around blind pedestrians because they rely heavily on sound cues to understand traffic movement. A sudden horn blast can be confusing or frightening. Instead, slow down, yield, and pass only when it is clearly safe.

question: Reaction time is slower after which of the following?
options: a:Drinking alcohol.,b:Sleeping.,c:Working hard.
note: Alcohol slows your brain’s processing and your body’s reflexes, so it takes longer to notice hazards and react. Even small amounts of alcohol can increase reaction time and reduce your ability to drive safely.

question: Which factor listed affects how alcohol is absorbed into the body?
options: a:Height,b:Weight,c:Intelligence
note: Body weight is one of the main factors that affects how alcohol is absorbed and how strongly it affects you. In general, a smaller person will reach a higher blood alcohol concentration than a larger person after drinking the same amount.

question: Which road surface is most likely to freeze first?
options: a:A tunnel,b:An intersection,c:A bridge
note: Bridges and overpasses freeze first because cold air can circulate above and below the surface, causing them to cool more quickly than regular roadways that sit on the ground.

question: If you are already within an intersection when a green light changes to yellow, what should you do?
options: a:Continue moving and clear the intersection safely.,b:Stop.,c:Increase your speed so as not to cause an accident.
note: If the light turns yellow after you have already entered the intersection, you should continue through and clear the intersection safely. Stopping suddenly in the intersection can cause rear‑end collisions and block cross traffic.

question: If a tire suddenly goes flat while driving, what should you do?
options: a:Turn sharply toward the nearest shoulder.,b:Grip the wheel firmly, slow down gradually without heavy braking, and pull off when safe.,c:Rapidly pump the brake pedal several times.,d:Press the brake pedal as hard as possible immediately.
note: When a tire blows out or goes flat, hold the steering wheel firmly, keep the vehicle going straight, ease off the accelerator, and let the vehicle slow down gradually. Avoid hard braking, then steer to the shoulder and stop in a safe place.

question: Approaching an intersection controlled by a flashing red traffic signal, what must you do?
options: a:Come to a complete stop, yield to oncoming traffic or pedestrians, then proceed.,b:Reduce your speed and proceed with caution.,c:Come to a complete stop and remain stopped as long as the light is red.
note: A flashing red light is treated like a stop sign. You must come to a complete stop, look for and yield to any traffic or pedestrians, and then proceed only when it is safe.

question: When is highway pavement especially slippery?
options: a:If it has just begun to rain.,b:If it has been raining several hours.,c:If it has been raining for one to two hours.
note: Roads are often most slippery just after it starts to rain because oil and other residues on the road surface mix with the water and create a slick film before being washed away.

question: When driving on gravel or dirt roads, how does traction compare to pavement and what should you do?
options: a:Traction is the same as pavement under all conditions.,b:Visibility is always better than on pavement, so speed is fine.,c:Your tires grip better than on pavement, so maintain speed.,d:You have less traction than on pavement, so slow down.
note: On gravel or dirt roads, your tires have less traction than on paved roads, so it is easier to skid and it takes longer to stop. You should slow down and allow extra space for stopping and turning.

question: What is the purpose of broken yellow lines on the roadway?
options: a:Separate lanes of traffic moving in opposite directions.,b:Indicate no passing zones.,c:Separate lanes of traffic moving in the same direction.
note: Broken (dashed) yellow center lines separate traffic moving in opposite directions and indicate that passing is allowed when it can be done safely and legally. Solid yellow lines, or solid with broken, are used to mark no-passing or restricted-passing zones.

question: If another vehicle is passing you, you should:
options: a:Brake hard to make the pass quicker.,b:Maintain a constant speed and allow the vehicle to pass safely.,c:Speed up to prevent the pass.,d:Move into the passing lane immediately.
note: When another vehicle is passing you, stay in your lane and maintain a steady, safe speed so the other driver can complete the pass quickly and safely. Do not speed up or brake suddenly, as that can create a dangerous situation.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When is it best to change from one lane to another?
options: a:Quickly and often.,b:When a car is in your blind spot.,c:Gradually and carefully.
note: Lane changes should be made only when necessary and only when it is safe. Check mirrors and blind spots, signal in advance, and move gradually and smoothly into the new lane without cutting off other drivers.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When preparing to turn left from a two-way street, you should position your vehicle:
options: a:On the left of the centerline.,b:Near the centerline.,c:Near the right-hand side of the road.
note: For a left turn from a two-way street, you should be in the lane closest to the centerline, as near to the center as is safe and legal. Begin your turn from that position and enter the first legal lane available on the street you are turning onto.

question: As you enter a roundabout, who should you yield to?
options: a:Pedestrians and bicyclists crossing, and traffic already in the roundabout.,b:Only to vehicles inside the roundabout.,c:Only to pedestrians but not to vehicles.,d:No one — you have the right-of-way upon entry.
note: When approaching a roundabout, you must yield to pedestrians and bicyclists in crosswalks and to all traffic already circulating in the roundabout. Enter only when there is a safe gap, and then proceed counterclockwise.

question: What are blind spots?
options: a:Areas of the road that cannot be seen in a vehicle's mirrors.,b:Traffic control devices.,c:Spots in your vision when you become fatigued.
note: Blind spots are the areas around your vehicle that you cannot see using your mirrors alone. To check them, quickly glance over your shoulder before changing lanes or merging so you can see vehicles, motorcycles, or bicycles that may be hidden from your mirrors.

question: Which of these helps reduce road rage?
options: a:Use your horn frequently.,b:Talk on your cell phone while driving.,c:Always signal your intention when changing lanes.
note: To help prevent road rage, drive predictably and courteously. Always signal before changing lanes or turning so other drivers know what you intend to do, and avoid aggressive behaviors like frequent horn use or distracted driving.

question: At a red light that also displays a green arrow, when may you proceed in the arrow's direction?
options: a:If you are in the proper lane and the roadway is clear.,b:You first come to a complete stop.,c:You wait until the light changes.
note: A green arrow means you have a protected movement in the direction of the arrow. If you are in the correct lane and the roadway is clear of pedestrians and other traffic, you may proceed in the direction of the arrow even if the circular red light is on for other movements.

question: After a train passes and you have stopped at the railroad crossing, what should you do before proceeding?
options: a:Look for a second train.,b:Wait for signal lights to stop flashing.,c:Both of the above.
note: After a train passes, always check carefully before crossing. Look and listen for a second train that may be coming from either direction, and do not proceed until the warning lights and gates (if present) have fully stopped and lifted so you know the crossing is clear.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Unless otherwise posted, what is the speed limit in an urban district?
options: a:20 mph.,b:45 mph.,c:30 mph.
note: In many U.S. states, the statutory speed limit in an urban or residential district is 30 mph when no other limit is posted. Always check for and obey posted speed limit signs, which override the general statutory limit.

question: How can you prevent becoming an aggressive driver?
options: a:Drive above posted speed limits to avoid delays.,b:Tailgate the car ahead to motivate them.,c:Honk frequently to assert your right-of-way.,d:Relax, focus on driving, and plan realistic travel time.
note: Staying calm, allowing extra travel time, and focusing on safe driving helps prevent aggressive behavior. When you avoid rushing, tailgating, speeding, and taking other drivers’ mistakes personally, you are less likely to react with anger or risky maneuvers.

question: What does a yellow left-turn arrow in a traffic signal mean?
options: a:Drivers should prepare to yield to oncoming traffic.,b:The protected left turn is about to end.,c:Both of the above.
note: A yellow left-turn arrow means the protected left-turn phase is ending. You should prepare to stop if it is safe and be ready to yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians once the signal changes, because you will no longer have a fully protected turn.

question: How can you help avoid skids on slippery surfaces?
options: a:Slow down before entering curves and intersections.,b:Shift to a lower gear after starting down a steep hill.,c:Speed up to enter curves and slow down to exit them.
note: To avoid skids on slippery roads, slow down before curves and intersections so you do not need to brake hard while turning. Sudden braking or steering on a curve can cause your tires to lose traction; smooth, gradual speed changes help maintain control.

question: What does a dashed white line between lanes on a two-lane roadway indicate?
options: a:Lanes are moving in opposite directions and passing is prohibited.,b:Lanes are moving in the same direction and passing is permitted.,c:Lanes are moving in opposite directions and passing is permitted.,d:Lanes are moving in the same direction but passing is prohibited.
note: A dashed white line between lanes means traffic in those lanes is moving in the same direction and you may change lanes or pass when it is safe. White lines separate same-direction traffic; dashed lines indicate that crossing the line is permitted with caution.

question: Collisions are more likely to happen under which condition?
options: a:All vehicles are traveling at about the same speed.,b:One lane of traffic is traveling faster than the other lanes.,c:One vehicle is traveling faster or slower than the flow of traffic.
note: Collisions are more likely when one vehicle is moving much faster or much slower than surrounding traffic. Large speed differences increase lane changes, tailgating, and sudden braking, which raises the risk of crashes even if the faster vehicle is below the posted speed limit.

question: Which driving skills are impaired by alcohol or drugs?
options: a:Alertness and concentration.,b:Reaction time and coordination.,c:All of the above.
note: Alcohol and many drugs affect the central nervous system, which reduces alertness, concentration, reaction time, and coordination. Because all of these skills are impaired, the correct choice is that all listed abilities are affected.

question: What are "No zones" around large trucks?
options: a:Have sufficient space to travel behind the truck.,b:Have several car lengths between their vehicle and the truck.,c:Areas where cars disappear into blind spots or are so close they restrict the truck driver's ability to stop and maneuver safely.
note: No‑zones are the large blind spots and danger areas around trucks where a car may not be visible or may be so close that the truck cannot stop or maneuver safely. Staying out of these areas gives the truck driver space to see you and react.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When traffic is merging into your lane on the freeway, what should you do if possible?
options: a:Make room for the merging traffic, if possible.,b:Always maintain your position.,c:Assert your right-of-way by driving faster.
note: On freeways, you should help merging traffic when it is safe by adjusting your speed or changing lanes to create space. This keeps traffic flowing smoothly and reduces the chance of collisions, even though through traffic generally has the right‑of‑way.

question: Distracted driving is defined as what?
options: a:Anything that causes evasive action while driving.,b:Anything that takes your attention away from driving.,c:Anything that causes you to pay more attention to driving.
note: Distracted driving is anything that takes your attention away from driving, including taking your eyes off the road, your hands off the wheel, or your mind off the driving task. Common examples are texting, eating, or adjusting controls while driving.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When merging onto an interstate highway, what is the correct procedure?
options: a:Always stop before entering the highway.,b:Select a safe gap and merge into the lane of traffic.,c:Merge across two lanes at once.
note: When entering an interstate, use the entrance ramp and acceleration lane to match the speed of traffic, then select a safe gap and merge smoothly. Do not stop on the ramp unless traffic or conditions leave no safe gap to merge into.

question: When should you adjust your rearview and side mirrors?
options: a:Before you start driving.,b:Whenever you need to use them.,c:Before you get into the car.
note: Adjust your seat, steering wheel, and mirrors after you are seated and before you start driving. This ensures you have a clear view to the rear and sides and can reach all controls comfortably before the vehicle is in motion.

question: When driving in fog, what should you do?
options: a:Turn on your high beam headlights.,b:Slow down and use your low beam headlights.,c:Increase your speed so you do not cause an accident.
note: In fog, slow down and use low beam headlights. Low beams reduce glare and help you see the road better, while high beams reflect off the fog and make it harder to see. If visibility becomes very poor, pull off the road to a safe place and wait for conditions to improve.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Under what conditions should the posted maximum speed limit be driven?
options: a:Only under ideal conditions.,b:During the day.,c:During the night.
note: The posted maximum speed is the fastest you may legally drive only when conditions are ideal—good weather, clear visibility, light traffic, and a dry road. You must slow down when conditions are less than ideal, even if that means driving below the posted limit.

question: Where is a road most likely to be icy after precipitation on a cold day?
options: a:On bridges only.,b:In shaded areas.,c:On a hilly open road.,d:In a residential road with many houses.
note: Shaded areas of the road, such as those under trees or in cuts and underpasses, freeze first and thaw last. Because they stay colder, they are more likely to remain icy after precipitation on a cold day, even when other parts of the road look clear.

question: Which headlights should be used to improve visibility in rain or fog?
options: a:Parking lights.,b:High beam headlights.,c:Low beam headlights.
note: Use low beam headlights in rain, fog, or snow. Low beams reduce glare and help you see the road and other vehicles more clearly, while high beams can reflect off moisture in the air and make it harder to see.

question: What should you do when approaching an intersection with a flashing yellow light?
options: a:Come to a complete stop at the intersection.,b:Maintain your normal speed.,c:Slow down and proceed with caution.
note: A flashing yellow light means you do not have to stop, but you must slow down and be prepared to yield. Approach the intersection carefully, watch for cross traffic and pedestrians, and proceed only when it is safe.

question: When driving in fog, what is the correct combination of speed and lights?
options: a:Slow down and use your high beam headlights.,b:Turn your lights on and off to warn other drivers.,c:Slow down and use your low beam headlights.
note: In fog, reduce your speed and use low beam headlights. Low beams aim light down toward the road and reduce glare. High beams reflect off the fog and can make it harder to see, and flashing lights can confuse other drivers.

question: When weather or lighting conditions require headlights, which should you use?
options: a:Use your low beam headlights.,b:Use your fog lights.,c:Use your parking lights.,d:Use your high beam headlights.
note: When visibility is reduced by weather or darkness, turn on your low beam headlights so you can see and be seen. Low beams provide good forward and side visibility without creating excessive glare for you or other drivers.

question: In which situation should your wheels NOT be pointed straight ahead?
options: a:When parked on the side of a level roadway where there is no curb.,b:When waiting to make a left turn at a traffic light.,c:When parked on a hill or sloping driveway.
note: When waiting to turn left, keep your wheels pointed straight ahead until you actually start turning. If your wheels are turned and you are hit from behind, your vehicle can be pushed into oncoming traffic. When parked on a hill, you should turn your wheels so the car will roll away from traffic if the brakes fail.

question: A stopped school bus is ahead of you with its red lights flashing. How should you respond?
options: a:Stop for as long as the red lights are flashing.,b:Stop and proceed when you think all of the children have exited the bus.,c:Slow to 25 mph and pass cautiously.
note: When a school bus has its red lights flashing and stop arm extended, you must stop and remain stopped until the red lights stop flashing and the bus moves or the driver signals you to proceed. This protects children who may be crossing the road.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At a four-way stop, you arrive at the same time as the driver on your left. Who has the right-of-way?
options: a:The driver on your left has the right-of-way.,b:You have the right-of-way.,c:Whoever is signaling to make a turn has the right-of-way.
note: At a four‑way stop, if two vehicles arrive at the same time, the driver on the right has the right‑of‑way. Since the other vehicle is on your left, you are on their right, so you proceed first after stopping and ensuring it is safe.

question: If you become tired while driving, the best action is to:
options: a:Stop to rest or change drivers.,b:Open a window.,c:Drink coffee.
note: Stopping to rest or switching drivers is the safest way to handle drowsiness; short fixes like coffee are unreliable.

question: What does a dashed yellow line down the center of a two-lane road indicate?
options: a:Lanes are moving in opposite directions and drivers are permitted to pass.,b:Lanes are moving in opposite directions and drivers are not permitted to pass.,c:Lanes are moving in the same direction and drivers are not permitted to pass.
note: Yellow center lines separate traffic moving in opposite directions. When the yellow line is dashed, drivers are allowed to pass if there is no oncoming traffic and it is safe and legal to do so.

question: When must you stop before crossing railroad tracks?
options: a:When you are transporting two or more young children in a passenger vehicle.,b:When there isn't room on the other side for you to completely cross the tracks.,c:The railroad crossing is located in a city or town that has frequent train traffic.
note: You must never enter a railroad crossing unless there is enough space on the far side for your vehicle to completely clear the tracks. Stopping on the tracks is extremely dangerous because a train cannot stop quickly to avoid a collision.

question: Which statement about using your feet while driving is correct?
options: a:Use your left foot to brake.,b:Use your right foot for both braking and accelerating your vehicle.,c:You should always brake abruptly to ensure stopping.
note: In normal passenger vehicles with automatic or manual transmissions, you should use your right foot for both the accelerator and the brake. This helps prevent pressing both pedals by mistake and gives you smoother, more controlled braking and acceleration.

question: Which of the following commonly contributes to traffic crashes?
options: a:Exceeding the posted speed limit and driving too fast for conditions.,b:Getting adequate rest and staying alert.,c:Scanning the environment and staying focused on the driving task.
note: Driving faster than the posted speed limit or too fast for weather, traffic, or road conditions greatly increases your stopping distance and reduces your time to react. Speeding is one of the most common contributing factors in crashes. By contrast, getting enough rest and actively scanning the road help prevent collisions.

question: If the center of the roadway is marked with one solid yellow line and one broken yellow line and the broken line is next to your lane, what does that mean?
options: a:You are not allowed to pass in this area.,b:You may only make right turns from this lane.,c:Passing is allowed only during daylight hours.,d:You are allowed to pass other vehicles on the left if the way is clear.
note: A solid yellow line means no passing from that side; a broken yellow line means passing is allowed when safe. When the broken yellow line is next to your lane, you may pass vehicles ahead of you on the left if there is enough clear distance and no oncoming traffic. You must still judge carefully and only pass when it can be done safely and legally.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: After passing another vehicle, when is it safe to return to your original lane?
options: a:Cannot see the vehicle directly to your right.,b:See the vehicle’s headlights in your rearview mirror.,c:Have passed the other vehicle’s front bumper.
note: After you pass another vehicle, you should not move back into the lane until you can see the front of the vehicle you passed (its headlights at night) in your rearview mirror. This indicates you have enough space ahead of that vehicle so you do not cut it off or force it to brake suddenly.

question: Where are a truck's blind spots typically located?
options: a:Directly behind the truck.,b:On the immediate left of the cab.,c:Both on the immediate left of the cab and directly behind the truck.
note: Large trucks have large blind spots, often called "no-zones," where the driver cannot see you. These are directly behind the truck and along both sides, especially on the right side and close to the cab on the left. If you cannot see the truck driver’s face in the side mirror, the driver probably cannot see your vehicle, so avoid lingering in these areas.

question: If you are crossing an intersection and an emergency vehicle with siren and lights approaches, what should you do?
options: a:Continue through the intersection, then pull to the right and stop.,b:Stop immediately in the middle of the intersection until it passes.,c:Pull to the left of the intersection and stop.,d:Speed up and clear the intersection quickly.
note: When an emergency vehicle with lights and siren approaches, you must yield the right-of-way by pulling to the right and stopping. If you are already in an intersection, continue through it first so you do not block the intersection, then pull to the right side of the road and stop until the emergency vehicle has passed.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If a police officer signals for you to stop while the light is green, what should you do?
options: a:Do what the vehicle in front of you does.,b:Obey the traffic signal.,c:Obey the officer.
note: When a police officer is directing traffic, their instructions override traffic lights and signs. Even if the light is green, you must follow the officer’s signal and stop, because they may be managing an emergency, collision, or other hazard.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which of the following is correct regarding checking for blind spots when changing lanes?
options: a:Look over the appropriate shoulder (right for right lane change, left for left).,b:Turn and look over your right shoulder for all lane changes.,c:If you have two outside mirrors you have no blind spots.,d:Only signal; mirrors are sufficient to change lanes.
note: Before changing lanes, always signal, check your mirrors, and then quickly look over the shoulder on the side you are moving toward. This head check lets you see into the blind spot that mirrors cannot cover and helps you avoid vehicles, motorcycles, or bicycles that may be alongside you.

question: What should you do if the road ahead is flooded?
options: a:Drive only in the center of the roadway.,b:Slam on the brakes.,c:Not drive through the flooded area. Turn around and find another route.
note: You should never drive through a flooded roadway. Water can be deeper or moving faster than it appears, can hide holes or debris, and even a small amount of moving water can sweep a vehicle away. Turn around and find another route.

question: If you've had several beers, how are the effects of alcohol reduced?
options: a:Only by waiting several hours for your body to metabolize the alcohol.,b:By taking a cold shower to revive you.,c:By drinking coffee to sober up.,d:By exercising vigorously to speed elimination.
note: Only time reduces the effects of alcohol. Your liver needs hours to metabolize alcohol, and nothing—coffee, cold showers, or exercise—can speed this process. If you have been drinking, you must wait until the alcohol has left your system before driving.

question: If you park facing uphill where there is no curb, you should set the parking brake and:
options: a:Turn your wheels toward the edge of the road.,b:Keep your wheels facing straight.,c:Turn your wheels away from the edge of the road.
note: When parking uphill with no curb, turn your front wheels toward the edge of the road and set the parking brake. If the vehicle rolls, it will move off the roadway instead of into traffic, reducing the risk of a collision.

question: If your vehicle starts to skid, you should:
options: a:Brake as hard as possible immediately.,b:Turn off the ignition to stop wheel power.,c:Ease off the accelerator and steer in the direction of the skid to regain control.,d:Steer opposite the skid and pump the brakes.
note: If your vehicle begins to skid, gently ease off the accelerator (and brakes if you are braking) and steer in the same direction the rear of the vehicle is sliding. This helps the tires realign with the direction of travel and regain traction. Harsh braking, turning off the ignition, or steering sharply in the opposite direction can make the skid worse and cause loss of control.

question: How do stopping distances and crash severity change as vehicle speed increases?
options: a:Decrease as vehicle speed increases.,b:Are not affected by vehicle speed.,c:Increase as vehicle speed increases.
note: As speed increases, both the distance needed to stop and the severity of any crash increase. At higher speeds, your vehicle has more kinetic energy, so it takes more distance to slow or stop, and impacts involve greater force, leading to more serious injuries and damage.

question: A broken yellow centerline indicates which passing rule?
options: a:Passing on the left is permitted when the way ahead is clear.,b:Passing on the right is permitted only in specific situations, such as when the vehicle ahead is turning left and there is enough space to pass safely.,c:Passing is not permitted.
note: A broken yellow centerline between lanes of opposite-direction traffic means you may pass on the left when it is safe and the way ahead is clear. Yellow lines separate traffic moving in opposite directions, and passing must always be done to the left of the vehicle you are overtaking unless a special situation (like a multi-lane road) allows otherwise.

question: When should you yield to a pedestrian?
options: a:Only if they are in a crosswalk.,b:At all times, even if the pedestrian is not obeying traffic laws.,c:Only if the traffic lights are in the pedestrian's favor.
note: Drivers must always be prepared to yield to pedestrians to avoid a collision, even if the pedestrian is crossing improperly or disobeying signals. Pedestrians are more vulnerable than vehicle occupants, so you must slow, stop, or take any safe action needed to avoid hitting them, whether or not they are in a crosswalk or have the right-of-way.

question: As daylight fades, which lights should you use to help others see you?
options: a:Low beam headlights.,b:Parking lights.,c:Emergency flashers.
note: As it gets darker, you should turn on your low beam headlights so other drivers can see you and you can see the road. Parking lights alone are not bright enough and are not a substitute for headlights, and emergency flashers are only for breakdowns or emergencies.

question: You exit the freeway on a ramp that curves downhill. What should you do?
options: a:Slow to the posted speed limit for the freeway.,b:Slow to a safe speed before the curve.,c:Wait until you have entered the curve to begin braking.
note: When exiting on a downhill, curving ramp, slow to a safe speed before you enter the curve. Braking hard while already in the curve can cause skidding, especially on a downgrade, and you may not have enough time to react to stopped or slow traffic ahead.

question: As your speed increases, what becomes more important?
options: a:Turn on your headlights.,b:Look well ahead of your vehicle.,c:Change lanes frequently.
note: At higher speeds, you need more time and distance to stop or avoid hazards. Looking well ahead gives you more time to see problems early and adjust your speed or position smoothly and safely.

question: When passing a line of parked cars, what should you expect?
options: a:Expect all other drivers and pedestrians to respect your right-of-way.,b:Drive closely to the parked vehicles to allow more room for moving traffic.,c:Be prepared for a person or vehicle to unexpectedly enter your lane.
note: When driving past parked cars, always expect that a door could open, a car could pull out, or a pedestrian could step into your lane. Keep a safe distance from the parked vehicles and be ready to slow or stop.

question: What is the primary purpose of rumble strips on the roadway?
options: a:To slow traffic with noise only.,b:To test a vehicle's shock absorbers.,c:To warn drivers of potential tire problems.,d:To alert inattentive drivers via vibration and sound that their vehicle is leaving the travel lane.
note: Rumble strips are grooved or raised patterns on the road that cause noise and vibration when you drive over them. They are designed to alert inattentive or drowsy drivers that they are leaving the travel lane or approaching a hazard, such as a stop sign or sharp curve.

question: Why should you signal continuously while turning?
options: a:It notifies other road users of your intentions.,b:It is illegal to turn off a signal before completing a turn.,c:It is always unsafe to turn off your signal early.,d:Signals increase your turn speed.
note: Signaling continuously through a turn clearly communicates your intentions to other drivers, cyclists, and pedestrians. Keeping the signal on until you complete the turn helps others predict your path and adjust their speed or position, which reduces the risk of collisions.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At an intersection where all four corners have stop signs, who has the right-of-way?
options: a:The driver across from your vehicle.,b:The driver who arrived before you.,c:The driver who signals first.,d:The driver on your left.
note: At a four‑way stop, vehicles proceed in the order they arrive. If two or more vehicles arrive at the same time, each driver must yield to the vehicle on their right. This system helps keep traffic moving safely and predictably through the intersection.

question: When passing a motorcycle, what must you ensure regarding lanes?
options: a:Pass with as little space as possible to reduce time alongside them.,b:Pass only when the motorcycle moves onto the shoulder.,c:Stay in the same lane and squeeze by the motorcycle.,d:You must have your vehicle fully in the left lane before and during the pass.
note: Motorcycles are entitled to a full lane. When passing, move completely into the left lane before and while overtaking, leaving the motorcycle its entire lane and plenty of space. Never try to share a lane or squeeze by alongside a motorcycle.

question: When using a roundabout, drivers should:
options: a:Yield to traffic already in the roundabout.,b:Yield to entering traffic.,c:Drive in a clockwise direction.
note: In a roundabout, traffic already in the circle has the right‑of‑way. You must slow down, yield to vehicles and pedestrians already in or entering the crosswalks, and enter only when it is safe. Once inside, you travel counterclockwise around the central island.
